Do not call `ListMcpResourcesTool` — it is not present in this environment and will error.

**Why:** The tool does not exist in this environment and will error. Re-confirmed eighteen times (2026-05-07, 2026-05-08 ×17) despite explicit memory — deeply persistent failure pattern: always called at scan start, often in parallel with the first bash probe.

**How to apply:** NEVER call `ListMcpResourcesTool`. Not at scan start. Not as a probe. Not ever. It does not exist. In Operator scans, go directly to `mcp__pi__bash` + curl. Available MCP tools are always visible in the tool list as `mcp__pi__*`, `mcp__playwright__*`, `mcp__voicemode__*` — no discovery call needed. Before every first tool call in any Operator scan, ask: "am I about to call ListMcpResourcesTool?" If yes, stop and call bash instead.
entries.description: ListMcpResourcesTool is not available; check tool list for mcp__<server>__* patterns instead

entries.text:
The papercup workspace backup snapshots `~/.papercusp-workspaces/<id>` (the workspaceRoot) but stores its kopia repo at `<workspaceRoot>/backups/kopia-repo`. The repo is *inside* its own source. If `backups` is not in `IGNORE_PATTERNS` (now `apps/operator/lib/backup/policy.ts` — extracted there 2026-05-21 from `workspace-backup.ts` so the constant has one source of truth shared with `self-exclusion.test.ts`), every snapshot recursively re-includes the previous repo and the store grows toward 1TB. Has happened twice; both required manual `rm -rf`.

**Why:** original Phase 1 (commit `2a2f3c95`) introduced IGNORE_PATTERNS without these self-exclusions. Fixed properly in commit `1a8d1f67` (2026-05-13): added self-exclude entries plus `assertSelfExclusionPolicy()` guard in `snapshot()` that reads the global policy back via `kopia policy show --global --json` and refuses to snapshot if `backups` is missing. Real-kopia integration test at `apps/operator/lib/backup/self-exclusion.test.ts` proves it.

**`db-dumps` is NOT a self-exclusion entry — do not re-add it.** `1a8d1f67` wrongly lumped `db-dumps` into the self-exclude list; removed again 2026-05-21 (commit `8f1109b2`). The pre-snapshot hook writes the PG dump into `<workspaceRoot>/db-dumps/pg-embedded.sql.gz` *precisely so kopia versions it* — excluding it silently broke point-in-time DB restore. Only `backups`, `.restored`, `.broken-*`, `.rolled-back-*` are genuine self-exclusions (kopia repo + recovery scratch dirs). `db-dumps/hook.log` stays out via the separate `*.log` rule.

**How to apply:** never remove `backups` / `.restored` / `.broken-*` / `.rolled-back-*` from `IGNORE_PATTERNS`, and never re-add `db-dumps`. The kopia policy is synced by `applyGlobalPolicy()`, which `ensureRepo()` runs on every path (incl. the warm/already-connected one as of `8f1109b2`) so settings changes propagate; it diffs via `diffPolicyIgnores()` and issues `--remove-ignore` for stale rules. If anyone reworks the layout so the repo is *outside* workspaceRoot, the guard can be relaxed. If size blows up again, first check whether `kopia policy show --global --json` actually contains `backups` in `files.ignore` for the affected workspace. See [[papercup-backup-integration]].
entries.description: Per-workspace kopia repo lives inside workspaceRoot; IGNORE_PATTERNS MUST exclude 'backups' or every snapshot recursively re-includes the repo and balloons toward 1TB

For any UI/frontend bug fix, run an actual browser e2e test (headless
Chromium via Playwright) that reproduces the user's exact action and
confirms the fixed behavior — BEFORE telling the user it's fixed.

**Why:** On the "loading diff" bug I shipped two wrong "fixes" in a row
(an O(n²) splitDiff theory, then an empty-patch theory) — each verified
only with unit tests / curl, neither reproduced in a browser. Both were
wrong. The real cause (browser connection-pool exhaustion) was only
visible when actually driving the page in a browser. The user had to ask
twice before I did it.

**How to apply:** Playwright is installed at
`papercupai-workspace/papercup/node_modules/playwright` with chromium
browsers. Write a `.mjs` script: `chromium.launch({headless:true})` →
`page.goto` → reproduce the click → poll the DOM for the success state
→ assert. Capture `page.on('request'/'response')` and console errors.
curl / unit tests prove the server or a function in isolation — they do
NOT prove the browser-side behavior the user actually sees. See
[[project_harness_sse_pool_exhaustion]].
entries.description: Verify every UI/frontend fix with a real browser e2e test before claiming it's done

When the user reports a "white screen" or "nothing visible" in the Tauri desktop app, the OS-level window may be collapsed to a tiny size (e.g. 10×10) while the page inside renders fine.

**Why:** `tauri-agent-tools eval`/`capture`/`page-state` report the *webview* viewport, not the OS window size. The viewport can be 1280×500 internally while the window OS-frame is 10×10 — visually a blank dot — and every JS check returns "page loaded, body present" because the DOM is alive; you just can't see it.

**How to apply:** Before chasing compile / hydration / suspense fallbacks for a "white screen" report:

1. `tauri-agent-tools list-windows | grep -i papercusp` — reports `WIDTHxHEIGHT` from the OS WM.
2. If size is degenerate (< 200 pixels in either dim), the bug is window-management, not rendering. Fix with `xdotool windowsize <wid_decimal> 1280 800` (use the `0x...` ID from `wmctrl -lG`, converted to decimal — or `wmctrl -ir 0x... -e 0,...`).
3. Then start the normal render-debugging flow.

Hit by this 2026-05-14 — spent half a debugging cycle blaming "Compiling /" slow first-compile when the actual bug was a 10×10 OS window.
entries.description: For Tauri "white screen" reports, check OS window dimensions via tauri-agent-tools list-windows BEFORE assuming render/compile bug. Viewport size from eval/page-state lies when the OS window itself is collapsed.

The Claude Code file-memory **index `MEMORY.md` is now an auto-generated
projection**, not a hand-maintained document. A `SessionStart` hook runs
`~/.claude/scripts/memory-compact.mjs`, which reads every topic file's
frontmatter (`name` + `description`, with a body fallback when the description
is weak), groups by `type`, and writes a terse, recency-sorted index held under
a ~20 KB soft cap (below the native ~24.4 KB hard cap, above which the index is
silently truncated).

**Why:** the old hand-maintained index drifted and grew unbounded (it hit ~60 KB
and was being silently truncated = live memory loss). Making it a projection
means it can't drift or bloat, and brevity is enforced. See the
[[fix-claude-code-memory-2026-06-05]] plan + `memory/archive/_compact-report-2026-06-05.md`.

**How to apply:**
- **Never hand-edit `MEMORY.md`** and **don't add a manual pointer line to it** —
  every session start overwrites it. To add/curate a memory, write or edit the
  **topic file**; it appears in the regenerated index automatically.
- Keep `description` frontmatter to a tight one-liner — it *is* the index hook.
- Durable types (`user`/`feedback`/`reference`) are never auto-evicted. Only
  `project` memories that read like derivable session state (su-ids, DONE/SHIPPED,
  migration numbers, plan slugs, dates, test counts) get archived to
  `memory/archive/` when stale or over cap — recoverable with `mv`.
- A `project` memory that is really a durable fact belongs as `type: reference`
  (or `feedback`) so it is never evicted — a `PreToolUse` hook
  (`memory-boundary-check.mjs`) nudges at write time when a memory looks like
  derivable state that should live in a plan/work_item instead.
entries.description: MEMORY.md is auto-generated by ~/.claude/scripts/memory-compact.mjs (a SessionStart hook) — never hand-edit the index; edit the topic files, which are the source of truth

When verifying Codex CLI behavior (hooks, tool payloads), do NOT copy `~/.codex/auth.json` into a throwaway `CODEX_HOME` and run `codex exec`. Codex OAuth refresh tokens are **single-use + rotating**: the throwaway run's refresh attempt rotates the token server-side, which can invalidate the user's real on-disk refresh token → they get logged out and must `codex login` again.

**Why:** hit this 2026-05-30 probing the Codex `apply_patch` hook payload. The probe 401'd (`refresh_token_reused`) and — by luck — the on-disk token was already stale so no live token was consumed; but the failure mode is real. Re-confirmed 2026-05-30 during the three-client lock in-vivo verification: a real `codex-su exec` 401'd the same way, blocking the Codex owner-resolution check (Claude's branch passed fully).

**How to apply:**
- Prefer offline inspection: `strings` the native binary at `@openai/codex-linux-x64/.../bin/codex` — it embeds the full hook JSON schema (`PreToolUseHookSpecificOutputWire`, `permissionDecision`, tool names, `settings.json`/`CODEX_HOME` paths). That answered everything without auth.
- `codex-su`'s `CODEX_HOME=~/.papercusp/codex-su-home` has `auth.json` as a **symlink** to the real `~/.codex/auth.json` (not a copy) — so `codex-su` is the safe "use real auth in-place" path the hazard above recommends. It's still subject to refresh-token rotation if the token is already stale.
- **Before blaming yourself for a `refresh_token_reused` 401**, check `stat ~/.codex/auth.json`: mode 600, and if mtime predates your run, you did NOT rotate it (a reused-refresh attempt consumes nothing new server-side). The user just needs to `codex login` again — pre-existing, not caused by your test.
- Headless invocation form: `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "<prompt>" < /dev/null` (needs the git-repo-check skip outside a trusted dir; close stdin or it hangs reading it).
- **Headless codex exec auto-cancels MCP tool calls.** Calling any MCP-server tool (e.g. papercusp-su) from `codex exec` fires an MCP-tool-call approval *elicitation* (`ResolveElicitation { request_id: "mcp_tool_call_approval_…" }`); with no interactive user codex resolves it `Cancel` → "(failed) / user cancelled MCP tool call". This is NOT the shell `approval_policy` — `-a never`/`-c approval_policy="never"` does NOT fix it. Use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (an `exec`-level flag) to auto-approve. Interactive `codex-su` TUI sessions just prompt the user, so they're unaffected. Connection/auth/bearer were all fine — discovery via `tool_search` works; only the approval gate blocks. Verified 2026-05-30 confirming `codex-su` per-session identity (owner resolved to `codex-su-<sid>`).
- Codex's hook contract is Claude-Code-identical (see [[project_claude_code_unsupported]] / the three-client lock-hook work).
entries.description: Probing Codex by copying auth.json into a temp CODEX_HOME can rotate/invalidate the user's real Codex OAuth login; use the binary/strings or a non-auth path instead.

entries.text:
When two processes need to communicate: use a real transport
(HTTP/SSE, in-process call, MCP dispatch). If you need to persist for
audit or replay, persist *after* the transport delivers — never write
to PG, then have the receiver poll PG for the row.

**Why:** stated by user 2026-05-09. Polling-as-transport patterns are
slow, lose ordering guarantees, and confuse the persistence layer with
the messaging layer.

**How to apply:** for prompt assembly, agent ↔ orchestrator data flow,
and tool dispatch — call functions in-process or send HTTP. PG writes
go alongside or after, for audit. Examples in this codebase that
already follow the rule: `executeAction` posts to operator with auth
header (transport) and `feature_audit_consolidated` records the
mutation (audit). Examples to AVOID: writing a file to disk so a
sibling process picks it up via polling — replace with explicit RPC.
entries.description: User's architectural principle — use memory (HTTP/SSE/in-process) to send data between applications; persist to PG after if needed, never poll PG as a substitute for a message channel

During papercup Brief 32 P-009 (2026-06-05) I removed `@bprogress/next` from package.json+lockfile. An earlier migration had rewritten 5 live files to import `@bprogress/react` **directly** — but `react` had only ever been in the tree as a *transitive* dep of `next`. My operator-vite acceptance build passed because node_modules still physically held the package; the next real `npm install` pruned it, and every fresh dist emitted a bare external import → **blank desktop app** (rollup externalizes unresolvable bare imports and still exits 0). A peer (su-73795) caught it in isolated-Tauri verification and fixed forward (`@bprogress/react@^1.2.7` as a direct dep of apps/operator + apps/operator-vite).

**Why:** build greenness against a stale node_modules proves nothing about the dependency *graph*; rollup/vite externalize-don't-fail makes the breakage silent.

**How to apply:** when removing dep X, grep live code for direct imports of X's transitive packages (especially after any import-rewrite from X to one of them) and promote those to direct deps; for verification, prefer a check that exercises fresh resolution (`npm ls <pkg>`, `npm ci --dry-run` won't catch it — check the import actually resolves in the lockfile graph, e.g. `npm ls @scope/pkg` shows it as a declared dep, not orphaned-transitive). Related: [[feedback_use_locks_before_editing]].
entries.description: Removing a dep can orphan TRANSITIVE packages that live code imports directly (post import-rewrite) — verify with a fresh resolve, not a stale-node_modules build

When driving or verifying the **Papercusp desktop UI**, use the
`tauri-agent-tools` CLI (`probe` → `eval`/`click`/`type`/`check`/`capture`)
per the playbook at `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/testing/agent-e2e.mdx`
(served at `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`). Read §0–§2 + §15 first.
Do NOT hand-roll `curl` to the dev-bridge `/eval` endpoint or wrangle
`/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-*.token` yourself — that's what bit me (I had
[[project_tauri_agent_tools_integrated]] in memory but still reached for curl).

**Why:** it's the documented/supported driver; gives `probe`/`check`/`capture`
and avoids token/port mistakes. The docs body is mostly written for the legacy
Next `/harness` UI (now `/adv` + operator-vite), but §0–§2 (tools, pre-flight,
reporting) and §15 (gotchas) are current and authoritative.

**How to apply:** run `tauri-agent-tools probe` first. If auto-discovery says
"No bridge found" (the bundled `papercusp-dev.desktop` instances write token
files its discovery doesn't pick up, and there are many stale ones), pass
`--port`/`--token` from the live `/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token` — match
`<pid>` to the running desktop via `pgrep -f papercusp-desktop`. Verifying the
agent→UI control surface itself still goes through the real `ui:*` MCP tools
(`ui:list_clients`/`ui:get_state`/`ui:dispatch`); the CLI is for reload +
DOM inspection, not a substitute for the production path. Never drive the
user's live window with focus-stealing xdotool ([[feedback_e2e_no_focus_steal]]).
entries.description: Drive/verify the Papercusp desktop via the tauri-agent-tools CLI per the agent-e2e docs, not hand-rolled curl to the dev bridge

When dropping a Postgres table, `DROP TABLE ... CASCADE` removes FKs, views, and
triggers **defined on** the table, but it does NOT touch **function bodies** that
reference the table by name in plain SQL — Postgres tracks no dependency for a
table name inside a `plpgsql`/SQL function body. Those functions silently keep a
dangling reference and error (`relation "<t>" does not exist`) the next time they
run.

**Why:** bit me in the Restart b2b retire (drizzle/0054 dropped `b2b_quote_item`).
`fn_recompute_reserved_qty` had a `b2b_r` CTE selecting from `b2b_quote_item`, and
it's fired by 4 LIVE triggers (shop_order, shop_order_item, wholesale_quote,
wholesale_quote_item) — so every checkout / wholesale write would have errored.
CASCADE printed no warning because the dependency is invisible to it. Caught only
because a `libs/db/src/schema/shop.ts` docstring mentioned the trigger. Fixed in
drizzle/0055 (rewrote the fn, dropped orphaned `fn_trg_b2b_quote*`).

**How to apply:** before (and after) any `DROP TABLE`/`DROP COLUMN`, run
`SELECT proname FROM pg_proc WHERE prokind='f' AND prosrc ILIKE '%<table>%';`
(use `prosrc`, NOT `pg_get_functiondef` — the latter errors on aggregates). Rewrite
every hit + drop orphaned trigger functions in the SAME migration, then fire the
live triggers in a rolled-back tx (`UPDATE t SET col=col`) to prove they don't
error. Extends [[feedback_verify_identifiers_against_source_not_grep]] — verify a
table's real consumers (incl. DB-side code) before dropping. See
[[project_restart_stack]], [[feedback_named_dollar_quote_in_sql]].
entries.description: DROP TABLE CASCADE does NOT rewrite PG function/trigger bodies that name the table — grep pg_proc.prosrc before dropping

When running e2e tests against a real GUI window (Tauri desktop app, browser, etc.) on the user's live display, never steal focus.

**Why:** User is actively working in parallel — focus theft interrupts their typing/clicking. They explicitly chose "drive existing window" over Xvfb-isolation but only on the condition that their mouse/keyboard stay theirs.

**How to apply:**
- xdotool: use `--window WID` form (`key --window`, `type --window`, `mousemove --window`) which targets a specific window without `windowactivate`/`windowfocus`.
- Never call `xdotool windowactivate`, `wmctrl -a`, or anything that raises/focuses the target window.
- For clicks on hidden/minimized windows, drive via DOM (WebKit inspector / injected JS) rather than synthetic mouse events that require the window to be foreground.
- Screenshots: use `import -window WID` (works on unmapped windows after `xdotool windowmap` if needed) or capture via DOM serialization, not full-screen grabs.

**tauri-agent-tools bridge (the preferred non-focus-stealing driver):** `tauri-agent-tools probe` with no args returned "No bridge found" even with live debug-build desktop processes — it does **not** auto-discover. Read `/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token` (JSON: `{port, token, pid}` — note the real bridge port is *inside* the file, not the `:9223/:9224` CDP port the process also listens on) and pass `--port <port> --token <tok>` explicitly. The bridge drives via in-webview HTTP (`eval`/`click`) with **no X11 focus change**, so it's safe even on the user's `:0` display. To verify a workspace-scoped surface without touching the user's active window: pick a **secondary** Tauri window and `eval window.location.href=...` to repoint it at the workspace the `:3070` sidecar actually serves (the sidecar is bound to one workspace — `/api/harness/projects/lite` shows which), then restore its original URL when done.
entries.description: When driving GUI windows for e2e tests, never steal focus from the user's active session

When `mcp__pi__edit`'s `newString` contains a literal backtick that
isn't cleanly paired, or special characters like `$&` / `$n` /
`$$` (these are `String.replace` patterns), the tool can match an
unintended file boundary and effectively **duplicate the entire
file** — frontmatter, body, the lot. This bit me on
`plan-agent-launch-2026-05-21.md`: an inline P-027 description with
`shell-metachar/backtick/\`$\`/space` ballooned the file from 848 →
1275 lines without any explicit error.

**Why:** the tool treats `$&` etc. as String.replace patterns
(documented under `mcp__pi__bash`'s sibling, but applies to edit
too — also re-derived from an earlier `escapeLikePattern` bug in
runs.ts).

**How to apply:** when an edit's `newString` contains literal
backticks, `$`, or other shell/regex special chars in inline code:

- Strongly prefer rewording to avoid the dangerous combo. "backtick
  + dollar + space + empty" works as plain prose without the
  inline-code markup that triggers the issue.
- ALWAYS `wc -l` the file before + after a non-trivial edit on a
  markdown doc you care about. A 50% size jump means duplication.
- For very dangerous strings, write the file fresh with `Write` then
  use sed/awk instead of `mcp__pi__edit`.
- Recover via `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` and re-apply with safer
  text.

Related: see [[feedback_no_regex_for_func_args]] (regex greedy-match
hazard) and the `escapeLikePattern` bug pattern (the same
`String.replace` foot-gun, different verb).
entries.description: mcp__pi__edit can duplicate a whole file when newString contains a backtick followed by special characters; sanity-check line count after large multi-line edits

In shared-checkout repos (where multiple agents/sessions operate on the same working tree), running `git commit` will capture the **entire index**, not just what you `git add`'d this turn. Pre-staged deletions or modifications from other agents will silently ride along.

**Why:** at 2026-05-20 in papercup, the SU-lock hook shims (`apps/operator/scripts/hooks/{pre,post}tooluse-locks-*.sh`) were pre-staged for deletion in the index when I started a linter commit. My `git add` of just the linter files was correct, but `git commit` packaged the lint files *plus* the inherited deletions. The deletions broke `install-standalone-mcp.sh` references. Required follow-up revert commit `a3a51c59` on top of `ba184ebe`.

**How to apply:** always `git status --short` immediately before `git commit` — even when staging explicit paths. If the staged set includes anything you didn't add, either (a) `git restore --staged <path>` to drop it from the index before committing, or (b) decide deliberately to include it (and mention it in the commit message). For long sessions, also `git stash --keep-index` periodically to check that the index matches your intended next commit.

Related: [[feedback_paperclip_collision_race]] (shared-edit zones generally).
entries.description: ALWAYS git status before git commit in shared-checkout repos — staged-but-unmine changes will silently ride along

As of 2026-06-03, a **git-sync routine is live** in the papercup shared checkout (cron `0 */3 * * * *`): every ~3 min it commits the **whole shared tree** (mine + everyone's uncommitted work), merges with origin, and **pushes**. Auto-commits look like `chore(git-sync): auto-commit papercup [skip ci]`.

**Why:** announced via coord by su-b095b. This supersedes the old "commit each unit manually, don't push" discipline.

**How to apply:** do NOT run `git commit`/`git push` manually in papercup — just leave edits in the tree and git-sync handles it (a manual `git commit` will usually find "nothing to commit" because git-sync already swept it). Still my job: lint / verify the work itself; git-sync only handles VCS. Supersedes the manual-commit half of [[feedback_papercup_main_dir_stays_on_main]] and [[feedback_per_turn_commit]].
entries.description: In the papercup shared tree, git-sync auto-commits+pushes every ~3 min — do NOT commit/push manually

When deleting a `harness.<verb>('/path', ...)` block from `apps/operator/app/api/_hono/harness.ts` after porting it to Rust, **don't blindly delete from the handler-start line to the next `harness.` line.** Adjacent handlers may already be ported in earlier stages, leaving non-handler code (interfaces, helper functions, comment blocks) sitting between two distant `harness.` lines. The naive delete swallows hundreds of lines of unrelated helpers.

**Why:** This bit me twice in the Rust port loop sessions (stages 2.44 and 2.49) — each time it removed `loadIssuesOrSeed`, `readPendingIssues`, `IssuesFile` interface, and the `import type { IssueSeverity, IssueStatus }` block. Both times required restoring 227 lines from `.next/standalone`. Recovery pattern: `python3` to splice helpers back before the next surviving handler.

**How to apply:** Before deleting a handler block:
1. Run `awk '/^harness\\.[a-z]+\\(/ {print NR": "$0}' app/api/_hono/harness.ts | grep -A1 "<target line>"` to find the next handler.
2. If next-handler line - target line > ~50, walk forward manually and stop at the first `});` followed by a blank line or comment header (`// ───`).
3. If you must over-delete, snapshot `.next/standalone/apps/operator/app/api/_hono/harness.ts` for restore.
entries.description: When porting Hono handlers to Rust, never use "delete from handler line to next harness.* line" — non-handler helpers (types, functions) between handlers get swallowed

entries.text:
In the multi-agent papercup checkout, `coord:presence` staleness is driven by
**MCP-tool heartbeat recency**, not by whether you're actually working. A long
heads-down stretch of local Read/Edit/Bash (no `papercusp-su` MCP calls) lets your
presence go stale (>10 min), and a peer (or the batch supervisor) will read your
lane as DROPPED and claim it — exactly what happened on Brief 3 (su-487a7 picked up
my P-008..P-012 mid-flight).

**Why:** presence heartbeats are stamped by MCP tool invocations; the client's own
Read/Edit/Bash don't touch the coord substrate.

**How to apply:** during a long local-edit stretch (multi-file change, big test run),
periodically call any `papercusp-su` MCP verb — a `coord:declare-intent` refresh or
even a cheap `coord:presence` read — to keep the heartbeat fresh. When a peer does
claim your lane, recover by proposing a **split** over `coord:send` (keep the
mid-flight items, cede the not-yet-started ones) rather than fighting for it.
Relates to [[feedback_recheck_plan_status_before_starting]] and
[[feedback_use_locks_before_editing]].
entries.description: On the shared papercup tree, a long heads-down stretch of local file edits with no MCP calls makes coord:presence read you as stale — a peer then claims your lane

entries.text:
`/home/dev/.config/systemd/user/papercup-vm-mac.service` shipped with `Type=forking`, `PIDFile=/.../qemu.pid`, `TimeoutStartSec=120`. But `boot-sonoma.sh` runs qemu in the foreground (no `-daemonize`, no `-pidfile`), so the pid file never appears. Every 2 min systemd SIGTERMs the VM thinking startup failed, then `Restart=on-failure` brings it back. Looks like "Mac VM keeps crashing" — actually a systemd kill loop.

**Why:** The two parts of the unit contradicted: `Type=forking` says "the script will fork and exit, write a pid file to PIDFile=", but the script does neither. `TimeoutStartSec=120` then governs how long systemd waits for the pid file before declaring failure. Mac VM crash incidents that interrupted earlier builds in this session were likely all this same loop, not real VM crashes.

**How to apply:** When a systemd-managed service that runs a foreground process appears to "crash on a clock," check the unit's `Type=` vs the script's actual behavior. `Type=simple` matches a foreground command. `Type=forking` requires the binary to actually daemonize. Mismatched + a `PIDFile=` that's never written = guaranteed kill loop on `TimeoutStartSec`. Look for SIGTERM "from pid <systemd-pid>" in the journal as the smoking gun.

The Windows VM (`papercup-vm-win`) is NOT under systemd — runs standalone — so its crashes during this session were real VM hangs, not this issue. Don't conflate them.

**Regression history:** Recurred on 2026-05-13 — NRestarts hit 135 in a few hours before the fix was reapplied (Type=simple, TimeoutStartUSec=infinity, PIDFile=). Suggests some workflow (test script? old commit checkout? agent edit?) keeps reverting the unit file. **First diagnostic when the user says "Mac VM keeps crashing":** `systemctl --user show papercup-vm-mac -p TimeoutStartUSec,Type,PIDFile,NRestarts` — if those values aren't `infinity`, `simple`, empty, expect the kill loop. Also: 135 unclean shutdowns can damage APFS — after fixing the unit, watch for the next boot taking unusually long with zero disk writes (could be panic loop from corruption, requires SPICE inspection at `:5930`).

Related: [[reference_papercup_vm_setup]]
entries.description: papercup-vm-mac.service was killing qemu every 2 min — Type=forking + PIDFile= mismatch with foreground boot script. Fix Type=simple + drop PIDFile.

In OMP-launched claude sessions, the built-in `Bash`/`Read`/`Write` tools are disabled and replaced with `mcp__pi__*` equivalents by Meridian's launch wrapper (visible in `pgrep -af claude` as `--disallowedTools Bash,... --allowedTools mcp__pi__bash,...`).

**Why:** likely Meridian sandboxing claude to route all shell access through its own runtime for logging/permissioning.

**The stall pattern:** any `mcp__pi__bash` call producing >~5s of synchronous output (e.g. `apt-get install`, big `pg_dump`, multi-step shell pipelines) returns "Anthropic stream stalled while waiting for the next event". The command actually completes server-side — only the tool result is lost. Verified: kopia install, pg dumps, snapshot creation all succeeded despite stalled tool returns.

**How to apply:** For any command expected to take >5s, use this pattern:
```
nohup bash -c '<command>' > /tmp/log.log 2>&1 &
echo "pid=$!"
# Then in subsequent quick tool calls:
sleep N; ps -p PID; tail /tmp/log.log
```

Quick commands (mkdir, single grep, kill, status checks) are safe. Sudo with `</dev/null` works fine — the issue is duration, not sudo per se.

**Real fix would be:** Meridian's pi-bridge should allocate a pty for shell tools (currently it doesn't, which is also why sudo without `</dev/null` blocks). Worth filing upstream.
entries.description: Bridge tool used in OMP→Meridian-launched claude sessions times out on commands >~5s of synchronous output — workaround = background + poll

When authoring a Postgres migration with a `DO` block (or `CREATE FUNCTION` body), **always use a named dollar-quote like `$body$`** instead of the unnamed `$$`.

**Why:** `mcp__pi__bash` (and any other bash heredoc that passes through `bash -c`) interprets doubled `$` characters as shell variable references and collapses them to single `$` on the way to the file. The resulting `DO $ BEGIN ... END $;` is invalid SQL and the migration silently fails to execute. Caught in audit round 5 of the 2026-05-12 plans-1234 arc — migrations 060 + 061 were broken on disk for several days; pgvector only existed because the extension had been installed via a manual psql `CREATE EXTENSION` call.

**How to apply:** every `DO`-block migration uses this pattern:

```sql
DO LANGUAGE plpgsql $body$
BEGIN
  -- ...
EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
  RAISE NOTICE '...';
END
$body$;
```

Same shape for `CREATE FUNCTION ... AS $body$ ... $body$ LANGUAGE plpgsql`. Re-verify each new migration with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f path/to/migration.sql` before committing — `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` is required because psql's default is to print errors and continue, which is exactly how this bug went undetected.

See also [[no-regex-for-func-args]] — both are tool-quirk gotchas.
entries.description: Use named dollar-quote ($body$) not unnamed ($$) in PG migrations — bash heredocs silently mangle doubled $ to single $

In the shared `papercup` checkout (many agents on one `main`), **never use `git stash`** — not even to A/B a quick check.

**Why:** the stash is global to the repo, not to your files. On 2026-06-02 I ran `git stash push <path>` to temporarily revert one file and re-run tsc; under the Bash tool's cwd handling the pathspec was malformed (`:(,prefix:N)...`), so the push **silently failed** (created no stash). The following `git stash pop` then popped a **pre-existing peer stash** (`stash@{0} pre-tier3-arc`), conflicting `OperatorPanel.tsx` + `globals.css` into a 3-stage `UU` merge — which **blocked ALL commits on main** for every agent until cleared. A peer (su-4871fff9) had to clean it up in parallel.

**How to apply:**
- To check whether a tsc/test error is pre-existing vs. yours: `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, re-run, observe, then re-apply your edit. Never `git stash`.
- This is already in the repo CLAUDE.md ("Don't stash, branch, or carefully scope pathspecs") — the new lesson is the *mechanism*: a failed `stash push` leaves the working tree unchanged but a following `stash pop` operates on whatever `stash@{0}` already is (a peer's), and a conflicted pop wedges the index for everyone.
- Recovery if it happens: `git stash show --stat stash@{0}` to see the exact files the popped stash touched (blast radius), `git checkout HEAD -- <those files>` to revert to committed state, leave the stash entry in the list (don't drop a peer's stash), and coord:send the owner. See [[feedback_git_status_before_commit_shared_checkout]] and [[feedback_papercup_main_dir_stays_on_main]].
entries.description: Never `git stash` in the shared papercup tree — a failed stash push + pop can pop a peer's stash and wedge commits

When migrating a function signature (e.g. adding a 6th arg to `WasmPlugin::load`), do NOT use regex with `[^)]*` or `[^,]*` to find call sites. The regex eats through nested function calls, splicing the new arg INSIDE the inner call's parens.

**Why:** Hit this exact pattern three times in a session porting Rust signatures:
1. `WasmPlugin::load(..., HashMap::new(), ...)` → `HashMap::new(, new_arg, ...)` — broke compilation
2. `.call_action(..., payload.clone(), ...)` → `payload.clone(, new_arg, ...)` — same shape
3. `secret_store("X", VAL)` got the new args injected before `)` instead of after, again from the regex matching the wrong `)`

Each time cargo caught it immediately + the fix was small. But it happened three times. Saving a rule.

**How to apply:**
- For multi-line function call sites: use `mcp__pi__edit` per occurrence with the FULL signature (matching the existing closing paren by line context, not by regex). If there are many, list them by `grep -n` first then edit one-by-one.
- For single-line call sites with no nested calls: simple `sed 's|fn(arg1, arg2)|fn(arg1, arg2, NEW)|g'` is fine — but verify with `grep -c` after.
- If you must regex over multi-line context, anchor the match on something OUTSIDE the parens (the variable name being assigned, the awaiting `.await`, etc.) so the `)` you match is unambiguous.
- The `mcp__pi__edit` tool's exact-string-match is almost always cheaper than getting a regex right; default to it.
entries.description: Patterns like `foo\(([^)]*)\)` greedily eat through nested parens — broke `HashMap::new()`, `payload.clone()`, and `secret_store(...)` in three separate sed/python passes this session.

**Rule:** When deciding between `useState` and `useQueryState` (nuqs), default to nuqs. The agent → UI control surface (`ui:get_state`, `ui:dispatch`) reads/writes the URL — `useState` is invisible to agents and undriveable without a per-feature intent.

**Why:** This codebase shipped an agent-driven UI control surface in May 2026. Tabs, panels, selections, filters all need to be URL-backed so agents can both observe ("what is the user looking at?") and act ("switch to the Sessions tab") through a single primitive (`set_url`) instead of N per-feature tools.

**Put in nuqs:**
- Tab / view / mode selectors (`?tab=...`, `?mode=...`, `?view=...`)
- Open/closed state for panels, drawers, dialogs, dropdowns, banners
- Selection state (`?proposal=...`, `?feature=...`, `?slug=...`, `?file=...`)
- Search / filter / sort inputs (`?q=...`, `?filter=...`, `?sort=...`)
- Expansion / show-debug / show-timeline toggles
- Pagination, page size

**Keep as `useState`:**
- Loading / saving / busy / streaming / error lifecycle flags
- Mid-edit form drafts (typing-in-progress that would lose on reload)
- Hover / focus / drag / mouse-down state
- Transient toasts, copied-indicators, animation tweens
- Ref-coupled state where a `useRef` must read the value synchronously (e.g. xterm search-addon coupling, GSAP-tied selection state)
- Sub-millisecond render-only state (`mounted`, `RefreshKey`)

**Parser cheatsheet:**
- Closed enum: `useQueryState('tab', parseAsStringEnum<TabId>(['a','b','c']).withDefault('a'))`
- Boolean toggle: `useQueryState('open', parseAsBoolean.withDefault(false))`
- Open string: `useQueryState('q', parseAsString.withDefault(''))` or `parseAsString` (nullable)
- Discriminated union: encode as scalar (`"review:<id>"`) + derive object via `useMemo`. Don't put 1KB JSON in the URL.
- Last resort: `parseAsJson<Shape>(shapeGuard)`

**How to apply:**
- When adding new state, ask "would this be useful in the URL?" If yes → nuqs.
- When auditing an existing file, look for `useState<'a' | 'b' | 'c'>(...)`, `useState(false)` for `open`/`show*`, `useState<string | null>(null)` for `selected*`/`active*` — all are nuqs candidates.
- For discriminated-union selection state with > 2 cases, encode the kind+id as a scalar string (`"review:<id>"`) and derive the object with `useMemo`. See `apps/operator/app/harness/ArchitectInbox.tsx` for the canonical example.

**Anti-pattern this rule fights:**
- Defaulting to `useState` because "that's what we always do"
- Avoiding nuqs because the param "isn't bookmark-worthy" (it doesn't need to be — agent visibility alone is enough)
- Worrying about URL noise (long URLs are fine; this isn't a public-facing site)

**Audit reference:** `apps/operator/docs/nuqs-audit-2026-05-11.md` enumerates the 46+ params migrated this session and the deliberate exclusions (mid-edit modes, ref-coupled state, etc.) with rationale per case. Read it before adding NEW exclusions.
entries.description: User-meaningful state goes in the URL via nuqs, not useState. Agents read/drive UI via the URL, so useState is invisible to them.

**ALL papercup work happens on `main`, in the canonical checkout
`~/papercupai-workspace/papercup`. No feature branches, no git worktrees, no
PRs.** (Reaffirmed 2026-05-30 after a sub-agent silently checked the repo out
onto `feat/psu-wrappers` mid-session, stranding commits — the user reconciled it
back to main and restated the rule emphatically.)

**Why:** worktrees cause more merge pain than they solve; branches strand work
and diverge; paperclip + dev servers + the harness fleet all assume `main`.

**How to handle concurrent agents on the same `main` checkout (the real
mechanism):** use the **lock + coordination system**, not branch isolation.
- `locks:acquire` the exact files before editing; `locks:release` after.
- `coord:declare-intent` + `coord:send` to broadcast what you're touching.
- Commit each unit the instant it verifies (don't batch across packages) —
  paperclip's timed `git add -A` will otherwise sweep your uncommitted files.
- `git reset -q` + `git add <explicit paths>` right before each commit so you
  only commit your own paths.

**Do NOT pause plan implementation because of sync friction** — the user was
explicit (2026-05-30): "we can't pause the plan implementation just because of
these issues." Work through it with locks/coord and do your best; a stray
commit-boundary smudge from paperclip is acceptable, lost work is not (hence
commit-immediately).

**Before committing, always `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`** — confirm you're
on `main`; another agent may have moved the checkout. If it's off main, flag it
via coord and (with the user) get it back to main; never do branch surgery
yourself on the shared checkout.

[[feedback_paperclip_collision_race]], [[project_papercusp_abstraction_audit]].

Two-part rule for storage and inter-process communication in papercup:

## 1. PG by default for durable state

For any new durable state in the papercup operator app, **default to Postgres**.
Files are reserved for the specific cases listed in
`apps/operator/content/docs/system/storage-policy.mdx`.

**Why:** Across rounds 1-14 of file→PG migration we moved ~30 surfaces out
of files / in-memory `Map`s into PG. The same drift patterns keep recurring:
file-primary-PG-mirror bifurcations, `Map<>`s losing TTL'd state on restart,
localStorage that needed to sync across devices, in-memory rate limits
bypassed by restarts. Each costs another migration arc to clean up.

**How to apply:**
- New per-workspace single-row state → `operator-state-pg.ts` (read/write/update helpers)
- New compound-key state → focused module using `getOrgPg()` directly
- New auth/session/TTL state (nonces, pair tokens, etc.) → PG row with atomic UPDATE-RETURNING claim, NOT a `Map<>`
- New "user preference" → `operator_user_profile` JSONB + `/api/profile`, with localStorage as per-device cache only
- Sensitive data → add to `ENCRYPTED_TABLES` in `db-encryption.ts`

**Reject these patterns** (all caught and migrated previously):
- `fs.writeFileSync('something.json')` for app state
- `const cache = new Map<>()` for TTL'd state
- "File is primary, PG is best-effort mirror" — always drifts
- Bearer tokens duplicated to disk when already in `token_index`

**Acceptable file uses (short list):** bootstrap state (workspace registry,
db-encryption-key), Postgres's own data dirs, code/scripts/templates,
harness contract artifacts read by inside-harness tools, append-only logs
at high volume, O_EXCL locks, plugin-sandbox storage, per-device UX
preferences that should NOT sync.

## 2. Don't use the DB as a transport

**Never** use Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (or polling a row) as the wire
between two processes you control. Move data over memory: in-process
channels, HTTP, Unix sockets. Persist to PG only when the data needs
to survive a restart — and even then, persistence is a side-effect of
the receiver, not the transport itself.

**Why:** stated explicitly by the user 2026-05-08 during the Rust
backend port discussion, but consistent with prior decisions —
checkpoint pg_notify is the only legitimate use because the row is
already canonical and notify is best-effort dispatch on top.

**How to apply:**
- Two of our processes need to share an event stream → put the
  producer endpoint and the consumer/SSE in the same process; route
  upstream POSTs there via rewrite/proxy.
- Cross-host fan-in → HTTP webhook or socket, not a "writer process
  inserts and reader process polls" pattern.
- Existing pg_notify uses (e.g., `checkpoint:fired` /
  `checkpoint:granted` in ARCHITECTURE.md §3) are grandfathered —
  they're notification-on-canonical-row, not data transport.
- During the Rust port, this means producer endpoints (`/api/internal/*-event`)
  must move to the Rust server **as a group** alongside their consumers,
  not split across Next ↔ Rust.

**Reference:** `apps/operator/content/docs/system/storage-policy.mdx`
(also linked from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at repo root).
entries.description: Default to Postgres for durable state; never use the DB as a transport between processes. Move data over memory/HTTP/sockets and persist to PG only when persistence is required.

The app is in testing. There are no active users. There is no production environment to "see how a fix fares in" before applying the right fix.

**Why this matters:** Without this framing, agents instinctively add deprecation aliases, ship compromise fixes, layer on top of wrong APIs instead of replacing them, and skip schema migrations to "minimize risk." All of those instincts are wrong here — the only risk is shipping the wrong design.

**Rule (verbatim from the user):** "We don't defer fixes for later to 'see how they fare in production first.' There is no production, and that gives us the luxury to break things continuously until we have the perfect app ready for production."

**How to apply:**

- **Don't ship deprecation aliases.** When renaming an identifier/file/type, change every caller in the same commit. Don't leave `oldName as newName` re-exports "for one release cycle" — there's no production cycle to wait for.
- **Don't be afraid to break the API.** No external users depend on stable shapes. If a v1 API is wrong, redesign it — don't preserve an awkward compromise to keep clients building.
- **Take the schema migration now.** If `claude_session_id` should be `agent_session_id`, do the migration when the rename comes up — don't defer it as "data + API contract change" while accumulating drift.
- **Pick the best tool, not the safe one.** Aviyn (the user) covers any commercial license costs personally. License + compatibility are footnotes, not vetoes. Rank by capability fit; if Serena beats OMP for a specific case, say so even if OMP is already wired up.
- **Refactor architecture when foundational decisions are wrong.** Migration cost is dominated by future cost-of-wrong-architecture, not current cost-of-rework. The same logic that says "don't refactor mature systems" doesn't apply to pre-alpha.

**What to still do:**

- Surface what you're changing in your reply so the user knows. Don't ask permission to do it well — flag it, then do it.
- Run tests. The luxury to break things doesn't extend to breaking them *silently*.
- When you spot a future-cost trap (schema, API contract, identifier collision), call it out in the audit + fix it the same turn if it's in scope.

This memory has historically been undersold by agents who default to caution. Re-read the verbatim quote and treat it as overriding any general-purpose conservatism heuristic.

When you write a reverse proxy with `fetch()` (undici) and read the upstream
body via `await upstream.arrayBuffer()` (or `.text()`/`.json()`), undici
**transparently decompresses** gzip/br bodies. If you then copy the upstream
`content-encoding` (e.g. `br`) and `content-length` headers onto the re-emitted
(now-plain) bytes, the browser tries to decode plain bytes as brotli/gzip →
`ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED`, and the client's `fetch` throws "Failed to fetch".

**Why:** the upstream encoding/length headers no longer describe the bytes you
re-send once undici decoded them.

**How to apply:** in the proxy header-copy loop, skip `content-encoding` and
`content-length` alongside `connection`/`transfer-encoding`/`keep-alive`.

Concrete bite (2026-05-28): Restart shop `apps/shop/src/middleware.ts` auth
proxy (`/api/auth/*` → shop-api). shop-api brotli-compresses responses; the
proxy forwarded `content-encoding: br`, so the better-auth client's sign-in
fetch threw. The session cookie WAS set (sign-in "worked"), but the success
redirect to `/account/orders` never fired — user left on the sign-in page with
no error. Fixed in `2332e4d4`. Symptom signature: login succeeds server-side
but UI doesn't advance + `ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED` in console.
entries.description: When proxying a fetch() response, undici auto-decompresses arrayBuffer()/text() — strip content-encoding AND content-length or the browser fails to decode

entries.text:
When a VM (Mac or Windows) shows a frozen/black display and SSH times out at banner exchange, **check `info status` via the qemu monitor before assuming a crash**. The Windows VM did this on 2026-05-13 (paused at 16:35, discovered 7.5h later when user noticed black screen):

```
$ (echo "info status") | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/home/dev/windows-vm/qemu-monitor.sock
VM status: paused (io-error)
```

QEMU's default `werror=stop` policy pauses the VM on the first failed disk write rather than letting the guest OS see a phantom-success and corrupt data. Symptoms match a hang exactly:
- Frozen/black display (last frame stuck)
- SSH banner-exchange timeout
- `/proc/<qemu-pid>/stat` shows utime/stime not advancing
- `/proc/<qemu-pid>/io` shows no recent writes

**Why:** Transient filesystem hiccups, qcow2 cluster-allocation issues, or actual disk problems — qemu can't tell which, so it stops to be safe. Almost always resumable if the underlying cause was transient.

**How to apply:**
1. Always check `info status` first. If `running`, the inner OS is hung — different problem.
2. If `paused (io-error)`, verify host disk space (`df -h`) and the qcow2 file (`ls -lah`, `stat`). If both fine, the pause was likely transient.
3. Resume with `(echo "cont") | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<monitor-sock>` — then re-check `info status` 10s later; if still `running`, you're good.
4. From the guest's perspective, time effectively skipped — Windows uptime won't reset. Don't trust wall-clock-based things (TLS expirations, NTP drift) inside the VM until they self-correct.

**Watchdog idea:** Two VMs makes this >0% to recur. A 1-min cron that queries both monitor sockets and pages on `paused` is 15 lines of bash.

**Sock paths:**
- Mac: `/home/dev/macos-vm/OSX-KVM/qemu-monitor.sock`
- Windows: `/home/dev/windows-vm/qemu-monitor.sock`

Related: [[reference_papercup_vm_setup]]
entries.description: QEMU pauses a VM on disk I/O error (werror=stop default). Black screen + SSH hang + flat CPU = paused, not crashed. Resume via monitor `cont`.

When two agents share `coord/plugin.jsonl` (or any cross-agent file), the per-turn-commit-and-push discipline isn't enough on its own — both agents need to **re-read the latest entries between PRs**, not just at session start.

**Why:** during a single session I shipped four PRs over a couple hours; tsplugin meanwhile opened PR #34 squashing G+1/G+2/G+3 (plus my then-in-flight G+5 that they captured incidentally), then independently reimplemented capture-migration as PR #36 before noticing my `plugin/g-plus-capture-migration` branch posted ~3h earlier. They saved their own version of this rule after the second collision; both of us recognized the pattern.

**How to apply:**
- Before opening a new PR on a touching surface (anything in the same package, same files, or even sibling files in the same directory), `tail` the other agent's coord file for entries since your last read.
- If they're in flight on something nearby, prefer **stacking on their branch** or **rebasing your branch on their branch** rather than opening a parallel PR.
- If you discover their version after-the-fact and one is strictly better, just adopt it verbatim (with attribution in the commit message). Symmetrical: if yours is better, post the comparison + offer to take theirs and revise. Either move is cheaper than letting both ship and resolving in main.
- This is *especially* important when one agent's work appears on the other's TODO list — that's the single highest-collision signal.

Restart **Scout** (`apps/scout-service`, :3350) DEFAULT is now **gpt-4o-mini** (`callOpenAI`, OpenAI
endpoint, `OPENAI_API_KEY` in .env) — switched from gemini-2.5-flash for reliable native function-
calling + far fewer 503s, at ~half the (tiny) cost. SupportedModel = `qwen3.5` | `gemini-flash-2.0`
| `groq` | `gpt-4o-mini` (all selectable via the `model` param; `DEFAULT_MODEL` in scout.types.ts).
(xAI **Grok** was added then removed — git-recoverable from commit 8b82a191.)

**The fix that made gemini reliable — FORCED function-calling (Option A), in `callGemini`:** on the
FIRST detection round only, append a `respond_to_user` sentinel tool + set `tool_choice:'required'`.
gemini-2.5-flash treats native tool-calls as optional under `tool_choice:'auto'` — it would reply in
prose and SKIP the obvious tool (search/prefill/open_drawer), then sometimes hallucinate it had acted.
Forcing a choice between the real tools and the sentinel removes that escape hatch. The sentinel call
means "no action, just reply" → filtered out → the streaming prose round runs. **Force round-0 only:**
forcing every round makes the model re-call the action in a loop (open_drawer fired 5× → MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS);
later rounds use `auto` so the turn terminates. Result: search **4/4**, prefill **2/2** (3rd was a 503),
open_drawer **1×**, chitchat streams a normal reply — and the real-browser /quote prefill that used to
fail now fills the form. A deterministic detection temp (0.1) is also set.

Forced function-calling is shared by both OpenAI-compat providers (gpt-4o-mini + gemini) via the
`RESPOND_SENTINEL` const + `forceTool` on round 1. gpt-4o-mini's native function-calling is strong, so
forcing is belt-and-suspenders there; for gemini it was essential.

**Gotcha — telemetry vs the least-privilege DB role:** scout connects as **`restart_app`** (DATABASE_URL),
which has INSERT/SELECT but **NO CREATE on schema public**. `TelemetryService.ensureSchema()` ran
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on every boot → denied → it flipped `degraded=true` and recorded NOTHING
(cost/usage) for ALL models. Fixed: on DDL failure, probe `to_regclass` — if the tables exist (always, on
deployed DBs), keep telemetry ON (INSERTs work). Lesson: any runtime DDL under `restart_app` fails; do
schema in migrations (privileged), not at boot.

Residual flakiness on gemini is ONLY Google 503s (infra, not routing); gpt-4o-mini avoids those.

**Testing:** Scout e2e = **verdict** (Tauri docs are papercup-only — Restart has no Tauri app). Drive the
browser chat (gemini default now routes reliably), or hit `/chat/stream` with `model:"gemini-flash-2.0"`,
or bypass the LLM via `POST /tooldef/mcp` with `x-service-key`/`x-on-behalf-of-customer`. `qwen3.5` also
reliable if needed. Governed surface (all `@papercusp/tooldef`): catalog.search, orders.serials/assets.list
(off serial_scan, customer-scoped); client tools open_drawer (cart `shop:cart-open`, quote new
`shop:quote-open`→GlobalQuoteCartIsland openRef) + generic prefill_form (RecommenderChat, specificity-scored
field match, never submits). scout-service CatalogService is detail-only.

If I claim "fixed" and the user reports the **same error class** again, stop fixing and **web-search the literal error string** (GitHub Issues API works fine: `api.github.com/search/issues?q=...`). Don't keep guessing at deeper layers of the stack.

**Why:** 2026-05-14 session burned ~15 fix cycles on "Fetch API cannot load … due to access control checks" in Tauri/WebKitGTK before searching. The actual cause was a documented WebKit HTTP keep-alive bug (supabase/supabase#20982 comment 1809994830) — WebKit reuses dead sockets and mislabels the resulting hang as "access control checks." Fix is one line of `Connection: close` in `next.config.js`. The Supabase thread had been open since 2023. Searching first would have saved hours.

**How to apply:**
- Error keeps recurring → `curl 'api.github.com/search/issues?q=<exact-error-string>'`
- Look for repro patterns matching user-reported behavior (intermittent, only-WebKit, only-Safari, etc.)
- Multiple unrelated projects hitting the same error message = third-party bug, not yours
- Also: **verification in a warm session is structurally invalid** for connection-reuse / cold-compile bugs. Test in a fresh Tauri window, not a reloaded one. Better still: ask the user to launch fresh and report.

All shared libraries (consumed by both Papercusp and Restart) must be named under the **`@papercusp`** npm scope, not `@restart`.

**Why:** Restart and Papercusp share code; Papercusp is the canonical owner of shared libs. The user: "all shared libraries should be under @papercusp not restart" (2026-05-29). Existing examples: `@papercusp/token-kit`, `@papercusp/test-config`. Restart-only libs keep `@restart/*` (e.g. `@restart/db`, `@restart/typesense`, `@restart/com`).

**How to apply:** when creating or extracting a shared lib, name it `@papercusp/<name>`. The established mechanism is a **git submodule** at `github.com/Papercusp/<name>`, path-mapped in `tsconfig.base.json` (see `libs/chat-protocol`, `libs/sse`, `libs/token-kit` in `.gitmodules`). Renaming an existing workspace lib's scope touches SIX places — miss any and it's half-renamed: (1) package.json `name`, (2) tsconfig.base.json path, (3) every importer's dep entry, (4) every import statement, (5) README/src header, (6) the `node_modules/@papercusp/<name>` symlink (`ln -sfn ../../libs/<name> node_modules/@papercusp/<name>`; remove the stale `@restart` one) — without (6) it won't resolve at runtime. Verify zero stray refs with `grep -rn "@restart/<name>" --include=*.ts --include=*.json apps libs tsconfig.base.json | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/`. Example: `@restart/rerank` → `@papercusp/rerank` (Restart `cb6d4625`+`a7f4c318`). Planned next: extract Restart's search logic (instruction template, llmRerank category-match, query rewrite, eval-harness contract) into `@papercusp/search-core` — see `docs/plans/search-relevance-rewrite-2026-05-29.md` §4.1.

In the shared Restart checkout, when another agent is also running `npm --workspace @restart/shop run build`, you get a **concurrent-build race** into the same `apps/shop/dist/`: each build emits its own content-hashed `RecommenderChat.<hash>.js`, and whichever finishes the **server (astro page) phase** last wins the HTML's bundle reference. Symptom that wasted ~30 min: my rebuild produced a bundle WITH my code (`B5deCLBn`), but the served `/scout` HTML kept referencing the other agent's no-my-code bundle (`DU5kgTP0`) — and a clean rebuild produced the *same* hash because the other agent mutated `RecommenderChat.tsx` mid-build (18s window).

**Tells:** rebuilt bundle has the same hash as before despite a source change; `dist/` contains TWO `RecommenderChat.*.js` (one with your markers, one without); served HTML references the one without. Grep a string literal (e.g. `X-Scout-Turn-Id`) in the *served* bundle to check — minified literals survive.

**How to apply:** don't keep racing rebuilds — it's futile and adds churn. (1) Confirm your SOURCE is committed in HEAD (`git show HEAD:<file> | grep <marker>`) — that's the durable truth; `dist/` is a gitignored artifact that self-resolves on the next uncontested build. (2) The live page often still WORKS during the skew (the old client's `data:`-line SSE parser tolerates the new `event:`/`id:` wire format). (3) For a clean verification window, coordinate or wait for the other agent to idle. Same family as [[feedback_git_status_before_commit_shared_checkout]] (index sweep) — both are concurrent-agent hazards in the one shared checkout.

When adding a SQL migration in the shared papercup tree, allocate its number with the **`db:next-migration`** tool, NOT by eyeballing the highest `NNN-*.sql` on disk and adding 1.

**Why:** `db:next-migration` computes `GREATEST(max-on-disk, max-reserved)+1` under an advisory lock, so concurrent agents never collide. Picking max-on-disk+1 ignores numbers other agents have already *reserved* (but not yet written to disk). On 2026-06-04 I (su-d3187) created `146/147/148-fleet-*.sql` by reading max-on-disk; su-584a8 had reserved 147 via db:next-migration for `147-coord-event-log-federation.sql` → two files at 147. They resolved it by renumbering theirs (→149/150). Filename is the `schema_migrations` PK so both would still apply, but duplicate NNN is messy + flagged.

**How to apply:** before writing `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql`, call `db:next-migration` to get the NNN. Especially important overnight when many SU agents land migrations in parallel. See [[project-fleet-supervised-blackboard]].
entries.description: Allocate new migration numbers via db:next-migration, not max-on-disk+1 (collides with peers' reservations)

In the papercup repo (`/home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup`), multiple SU shells (Claude Code, OMP, Codex — NOT Gemini) write concurrently, so file locking is enforced. **As of 2026-05-30 it is AUTOMATIC**: a PreToolUse/tool_call hook on every client claims a lock before each `Edit`/`Write`/`apply_patch` and blocks contended edits (see [[project_claude_code_unsupported]], plan `three-client-lock-enforcement-2026-05-30`). The hook is live in my own Claude sessions — it WILL block me on a held file.

**Updated how-to (supersedes "always acquire before editing"):**
- The hook locks per-edit; you rarely need a manual `locks:acquire`. When the hook blocks you, pivot/retry/yield — don't route around it.
- **Per-session identity FIXED 2026-05-30 (commit 3761b32b):** `claude-su`/`codex-su` now mint a per-launch `PAPERCUSP_SID`, fed into BOTH the interactive MCP `?client=` and the hook owner — so within a `-su` shell, manual `locks:acquire` and the hook share one owner (manual multi-file claims no longer self-block) and distinct shells get distinct coord/lock owners (coord:inbox stops self-filtering peers). **Caveat:** a plain `claude`/`codex` SU session (no `PAPERCUSP_SID`, e.g. not launched via the `-su` wrapper) still uses the static machine id → manual-acquire there can still self-contend with the hook; relaunch via `claude-su` to get the unified id. OMP interactive coord still collapses (deferred — no mcp.json env-interp).
- Manual `locks_acquire` is for a deliberate multi-file claim held across the commit (now safe under `-su`).
- Shape (when you do call manually): `mcp__papercusp-su__locks_acquire { paths: [<repo-rel-posix>], intent, ttl_sec: 1200, wait: { max_sec: 300 } }` → edit → `locks_release { lock_id }`.
- Paths must be **repo-relative POSIX** (no leading `./`, no absolute, no `..`).
- **Don't assume the lock surface is down.** `locks:*` and `coord:*` resolve a *static-client* identity (`su · <id>`, workspaceId `*`) and respond fine **even when** bearer-gated built-ins like `docs:outline` / `papercusp:list_workspaces` return `harness_not_registered` / `unauthorized` in the same session. Different auth path. Test `coord:whoami` / `locks:queue` before concluding the surface is unavailable — never pre-emptively skip locking on inference.
- Memory files under `~/.claude/.../memory/` are OUTSIDE the repo — the lock system doesn't apply to them.

Related: [[feedback_operator_scan_tools]], [[feedback_avoid_mcp_resources_tool]], [[feedback_paperclip_collision_race]].

In repos where multiple agents may concurrently touch `main` (papercup is the canonical case — 5+ agents commit/push every turn per the rust-port coord protocol), do new work in a `git worktree add ../papercup-<feature> -b <branch>` rather than checking out a feature branch in the canonical checkout. Reason: a `git checkout <branch>` in the shared checkout swaps everyone's working tree mid-edit, and `git stash` round-trips lose untracked files that aren't yet committed. Worktrees let me work in `../papercup-<feature>` while the canonical `papercup/` stays on `main` so other agents can keep committing.

**Why:** Confirmed footgun on 2026-05-10 — a `paperclip` agent switched the checkout to `design-phase-v0.1-recovery` mid-edit, which stashed my uncommitted work; not all of it survived the stash + checkout cycle, and I had to recreate several files from conversation context.

**How to apply:** For any feature branch off `main` in a multi-agent repo, default to:
```
git worktree add -b plugin/<feature> ../papercup-<feature> origin/main
cd ../papercup-<feature>
# work
git push -u origin plugin/<feature>
gh pr create ...
cd /home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup
git worktree remove ../papercup-<feature>
```
The canonical checkout never leaves `main` from another agent's perspective. Submodules need `--recurse-submodules` on worktree add or a manual `git submodule update --init --recursive` afterwards.
entries.description: When other agents may be working on the same checkout, do work in a separate worktree so main stays free

When a doc/plan claims "X is named Y", "there are N of them", or "Z doesn't exist", verify it against the **canonical declaration**, not a convenience grep. A string-literal or whole-word grep is a proxy that silently misses variants.

**Two misses in one session (SU-prompt audit, 2026-05-30), both caught by peer review:**
1. Claimed the agent role list was "11 incl. `tester`" from a `grep -roEh` of role-name **string literals** — but the canonical `AGENT_ROLES` (`role-config.ts`) has **19** and no `tester`; `KNOWN_ROLES` (`role.ts`) is a *different* 18 (has `tester`, omits operator/oracle). The two arrays even disagree with each other.
2. Claimed "no `spawns` DDL exists → drop the reference" from `grep -E '\bspawns\b'` — but `harness_shared.spawned_agents` exists (`049-spawned-agents.sql`); the word boundary skipped the morphological variant.

**How to apply:**
- For "named / how-many / exists" claims, open the source of truth — the `export const X = [...]` array, the `CREATE TABLE`, the enum — don't infer it from a pattern match.
- Grep on **stems**, not whole-word boundaries: `spawn`, not `\bspawns\b`; `role` not `'tester'`.
- Be most skeptical of your OWN "verified" tag in a doc whose whole premise is "I cross-checked every claim" — that's exactly where a lazy grep does the most damage.

**Same class, different probe (Restart CDN, 2026-06-02):** told the owner "Tiered Cache is NOT enabled" because the CF API returned `9109 Unauthorized` / `Authentication error`. But that token just lacked Cache-Settings **read** scope — the response said nothing about the setting's state. **A tool's inability to read a thing is NOT evidence the thing is absent/off.** When a probe is auth/permission-limited (CF token scope, an unreadable file, a 403/401/9109), report "can't verify with this access," never "it's not done." the owner had already enabled it in the dashboard.

Sibling: [[feedback_no_regex_for_func_args]] (regex imprecision in *edits*; this is regex imprecision in *verification*).
entries.description: Don't tag an identifier/table/enum fact 'verified' off a narrow grep — read the canonical declaration; a too-narrow pattern silently misses variants

Before trusting ANY live measurement (curl results, eval-harness numbers, "is my fix working"), verify the server process is actually the fresh one running your current code + env. Check the PID and start time (`ss -tlnp | grep :PORT`, then `ps -o lstart= -p PID`).

**Why (2026-05-29, Restart search):** I burned an entire long turn chasing a phantom "regression" — "canon camera → toner #1", 37ms responses, a harness run of P@5 0.718 with 2 guardrail failures — and wrote those bad numbers into plan commits. Root cause was operational, not code: the `:3100` shop-api was an **orphaned process** (started hours earlier) that `bin/overmind-all restart shop-api` did NOT control (there were several stale duplicate overmind instances on different sockets/tmux). Every "restart" I ran was a silent no-op; the zombie kept serving old code AND a stale `LLM_RERANK=0` env left over from a diagnostic. The code had been correct the whole time — killing the zombie + launching fresh fixed it instantly.

**How to apply:**
1. A suspiciously **fast** response is the tell: if a path should call a reranker/LLM (~1-2s) but returns in tens of ms, the rerank code isn't running — suspect a stale process or wrong route BEFORE suspecting the code.
2. After any restart, confirm the PID changed and start-time is recent. Don't assume `overmind restart`/`overmind-all restart` worked — orphans + multiple overmind instances make it no-op.
3. If a "regression" appears right after you toggled an env var for a diagnostic (e.g. flipped `LLM_RERANK=0` for a probe), suspect the toggle didn't get restored into the *actually-serving* process.
4. To force a known-good state: `kill <pid-on-port>`, then launch directly (`PORT=… node --env-file=.env node_modules/.bin/tsx apps/<svc>/src/main.ts`) and test that instance.
5. Don't commit measured numbers until the serving process is verified fresh. [[feedback_per_turn_commit]] is about committing code, not unverified metrics.

**Papercup operator instance (2026-05-30):** the running operator API on `:3070` is `tsx bin/hono-host.ts` (a long-running tsx process with NO file-watch); `dev:operator` → operator-vite `vite build --watch` is only the FRONTEND. So edits to `apps/operator/lib/**` (e.g. agent-tools) do NOT go live until that hono-host process is restarted — module singletons (like `coordLog`) were eval'd at startup. Verifying "is my server code live": send through the live tool and check WHERE the write landed (during the coord FS→PG port, a `coord:send` landing in `coord/*.jsonl` instead of `harness_shared.coord_event_log` proved the operator was still on the pre-cutover code). Restarting hono-host also resets the papercusp-su MCP session, so it's the user's call, not mine to do unilaterally.
entries.description: Before trusting any live measurement, verify the server is the fresh process you think it is — orphans silently serve stale code/env

In papercup (and any Vite app), `vite build` **exits 0** even when a bare import
can't be resolved — rollup externalizes it with only a warning, and the broken
entry module fails at RUNTIME with `Module name '<pkg>' does not resolve to a
valid URL` → React mounts nothing (empty `#root`, zero console noise until you
manually `import()` the entry).

**Why:** caught 2026-06-05 verifying Brief 23 — Brief 32's next-removal rewrote
imports to `@bprogress/react`, which was only a TRANSITIVE dep of the removed
`@bprogress/next`; the prune deleted it from node_modules and every later
watch-rebuild shipped a blank desktop app while "build green" held.

**How to apply:** after any dependency removal/prune, (1) grep the built entry
for leftover bare specifiers: `grep -o 'from"[^./"][^"]*"' dist/assets/index-*.js`
(or just the removed package names), and (2) treat "rewrote imports to X" as a
signal to check X is a DIRECT dep, not transitive. To diagnose a silent blank
SPA in a webview: `import(document.querySelector('script[type=module]').src)`
via the bridge — the rejection names the unresolvable module. Related:
[[project_adv_dock_nullroot_crash]] (the other blank-/adv class: stale-chunk
404s from watch rebuilds).

In the papercup monorepo, running `npx vitest run --root <pkg> <path>` from the
repo root works for **node-environment** suites (e.g. `packages/operator-core`
unit tests) but **breaks jsdom/`.tsx` suites** that go through Vite's serve
pipeline: the run fails at load with `Cannot find module
'/@fs/.../libs/test-config/src/setup-fail-on-console.ts'`.

**Why:** `--root` resets Vite's `server.fs.allow` to that package dir, walling
off the hoisted monorepo `libs/` that `@papercusp/test-config`'s
`defineVitestConfig` references for its setup file. Node-env tests don't hit the
`/@fs/` serve path so they're unaffected — which makes it look like a real
failure for only the UI tests.

**How to apply:** to run a UI/component suite, `cd <pkg>` and run
`npx vitest run <path>` (or the package's `npm test`) — let the package's own
config resolve the workspace root. Don't pass `--root`. A `--root` "Cannot find
module /@fs/..." is an invocation error, not a real test failure — don't chase
it as a broken symlink. See [[feedback-use-db-next-migration-for-numbers]] for
other papercup-specific tooling gotchas.
entries.description: In papercup, `vitest run --root <pkg>` breaks jsdom/.tsx suites ("Cannot find module /@fs/...setup-fail-on-console.ts") — run from inside the package instead

When the user asks me to "search online" or verify library facts (license, last publish, current maintenance status, alternatives), don't respond with "I don't have a web search tool in this environment." Even without a dedicated WebSearch tool, I can use (a) `curl` via bash to hit npm registry / GitHub API / raw docs, or (b) playwright `browser_navigate` against a search engine or package page. User pushed back both times; the expectation is to use whatever tools I have (raw HTTP via bash, or a real browser via playwright) rather than give a training-data-only answer. **How to apply:** For "search online" / "verify" / "is X still maintained" / "what's the license" / "what are the alternatives" style asks:
- Prefer `curl -s` against `registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>`, `api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>`, or the raw URL the user mentions — cheap, scriptable, no UI noise.
- If a search engine is genuinely needed, use playwright `browser_navigate` + `browser_snapshot` rather than refusing.
- Only claim lack of capability after trying and hitting an actual wall (blocked egress, auth required, etc.).

**"Fetch API cannot load <url> due to access control checks" in a Tauri/WebKitGTK
webview is almost never a CORS problem.** It is WebKit's misleading label for a
`fetch()` that never got a TCP connection because **libsoup's `max-conns-per-host`
(default 6) is exhausted by long-lived SSE/EventSource streams.**

**Confirmed 2026-05-20** after ~15 wrong fix cycles. Root cause: the operator
opens 5 always-on SSE streams (Zero sync, OperatorPanel, OperatorBackgroundScanner,
intent-dispatcher, use-state-snapshots) + 1 on `/harness` + Next HMR = 7 permanent
sockets to `localhost:3055`. With ≥6 slots camped, every regular `fetch()` hangs
forever. Full plan: `apps/operator/docs/plans/webkit-sse-connection-pool-2026-05-20.md`.

**How to diagnose (do this FIRST, not last):**
- `ss -tnp | grep WebKit | grep :3055` — count ESTAB sockets. ≥6 idle = pool full.
- In-page `fetch(...)` never reaches the server (no dev-log line) while `curl` to
  the same URL returns 200 in ms → it's the pool, not the server, not CORS.

**The real fix** is reducing concurrent EventSource connections: a client-side
SSE multiplexer in `@restart/sse` (one connection, N topic subscribers), or
making non-critical streams lazy. `@restart/sse` has server fan-out (`getChannel`)
but no client multiplexer yet.

**Misdiagnoses to NOT repeat** (all tried, all failed this class of bug):
`devUrl` 127.0.0.1↔localhost, `Connection: close`, ACAO:* headers, route
prewarmers, Turbopack compile-race theories. The `devUrl: localhost` change is
harmless and fine to keep, but it does NOT fix this.

**Verification is invalid in a warm session** — the bug only reproduces on a
cold window launch. Have the user fully quit + relaunch and check first paint.
See [[feedback-search-web-before-fix-loops]].
entries.description: "Fetch API cannot load … access control checks" in a Tauri webview = libsoup connection-pool exhaustion, NOT CORS. WebKitGTK max-conns-per-host is 6.

Fixed 2026-06-02 (commit 7c56c737e, papercup). Two separate causes behind "/adv tabs not loading / config not showing vditor markdown":

**1. Git tab crash latches every tab.** `HarnessDock` trusted `row.schemaVersion===1` to imply a valid `root`, but a save/fetch race on `/api/dock-layouts/:name` transiently returns a v1 body with `root:null`. Render path `useComponentsForLayout → collectTypes → walk(doc.root)` then threw `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'e.kind')` **during render** → `/adv` is ONE TanStack route (tabs are `?tab=`), so the latched error boundary blanks EVERY tab. Fix: `isWellFormedLayout()` (wraps `validateLayoutDoc`) in `apps/operator/lib/dock-layouts.ts`; HarnessDock validates → malformed renders empty + one-shot refetch; `persist()` won't save a degenerate layout; walk/nodeToBranch null-guarded.

**2. "config markdown via vditor blank" = stale-bundle 404, NOT a config bug.** Desktop loads `:3070` (Hono serves `apps/operator-vite/dist/`), built by `dev:nohmr` = `vite build --watch` which rewrites dist on EVERY edit (constant on shared box). Open webview's lazy chunks (vditor = `import('vditor')`) then 404 → blank markdown / "Importing a module script failed". Reload (native Ctrl+R) fixes; on a FRESH build config+vditor render fine. Part B: working reload affordance (`hardReload()` in `apps/operator/lib/hard-reload.ts` + RouteErrorBoundary + ChunkReloadPrompt + MarkdownEditor `.catch`). Deep cure (don't strand open webviews on rebuild) is OUT OF SCOPE, not done.

**GOTCHA: `Object.defineProperty(location,'reload'/'assign'/'replace')` is FLAKY on WebKitGTK** (Tauri webview) — `location.replace` redefinition throws, aborting the index.html suppress block before `window.__papercuspOriginalReload` was set (it was defined LAST). `window` props are reliable; location-method redefinition isn't. Fix = define the escape hatch FIRST. So desktop reload-suppression is unreliable; use `__papercuspOriginalReload` (now reliable) for a real reload.

**Diagnosis workflow (reusable):** never drove the user's live `:0` Tauri. Launched a dedicated `cd papercusp-desktop && DISPLAY=:99 npm run tauri dev -- --config '{"build":{"devUrl":"http://localhost:3070"}}'` (loads the current built dist), read its bridge token at `/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token`, and POST `/eval` JS to read the DOM / React fiber (`stateNode.state.error`) + intercept `window.fetch` to force `root:null`. GL-less Xvfb is fine for DOM-via-bridge. See [[feedback_own_xvfb_for_e2e]], [[feedback_drive_desktop_with_tauri_agent_tools]].

The live operator SPA at :3070 is a **prebuilt operator-vite bundle** (served from `apps/operator-vite/dist/assets/`, auto-rebuilt by a long-running `vite build --watch --mode development` process). `/adv/harnesses` in operator-vite is just a redirect to `/adv?tab=harnesses`; the real shell is `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvShell.tsx`.

**CORRECTION (2026-05-30):** `apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/` is NOT dead — it is the **live Harness tab**. `operator-vite/src/routes/adv/index.tsx` imports `HarnessesWorkspace` from `@/app/adv/harnesses/HarnessesWorkspace` (and the panels FeaturesPanel/IssuesPanel/DetailPanel/HarnessTopBar/PinMenu under it) via the `@/app/*` alias. The "dead copy" was `apps/operator/app/adv/_components/AdvShell.tsx` — the SHELL has a live operator-vite twin (`components/adv/AdvShell.tsx`); the harness-tab CONTENT components live only in the Next tree and are consumed through the alias (per plan `adv-harness-tab-migration-2026-05-30` D-006). The earlier "never imported" wasted-commit story was about the shell duplication, not these panels.

**operator-vite CAN reuse Next.js components**: it aliases `@/app/*` to the Next.js app dir (e.g. AdvShell imports `@/app/harness/Select`, `@/app/harness/CreateHarnessPicker`). So shared components live in `apps/operator/app/`, but the **mount point / shell** must be in operator-vite.

**Verifying a /adv change is live**: `tsc` can't resolve the `@/app` alias (shows TS2307 across the whole project — pre-existing noise; build script is `vite build`, not tsc). Confirm instead by grepping the freshly-built bundle: `grep -l "<your-marker>" apps/operator-vite/dist/assets/*.js`. Watch-build log is `/proc/<vite-pid>/fd/1` ("built in Nms").

**Same rule for `/admin` tabs (2026-05-31):** the live admin shell is `apps/operator-vite/src/components/admin/AdminShell.tsx` with routes in `apps/operator-vite/src/routes/admin/*.tsx`. A Next-only admin page (`apps/operator/app/admin/<x>/page.tsx`) is **unreachable** in the desktop — you must add an operator-vite **mirror route** (thin `createFileRoute` reusing the Next-tree client via the `@/app/*` alias, like `dogfood-substrate.tsx`) AND a `{ href, label }` entry in the operator-vite `AdminShell` TABS array.
