Desktop's Rust main writes `~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json` on embedded-PG ready (port, URL, pid, ts) and deletes on shutdown. Webapp `apps/operator npm run dev` reads it via `apps/operator/lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts` `getHarnessAdminUrl()` so both processes share the same DB. Connections from BOTH processes to the same embedded PG verified via `pg_stat_activity` (5 webapp + 2 desktop).

**Why:** user wants seamless web↔desktop dev on Linux without dump/restore — switch between Chrome :3055 and Tauri shell, see same data live (Zero/SSE handles change propagation; PG is shared).

**How to apply:**
- Never hardcode `localhost:5432` or `:16534` in operator code. Use `getHarnessAdminUrl()` from `lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts`.
- Resolution chain: `HARNESS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` > `DATABASE_URL` > `PAPERCUSP_PG_URL` env → discovery file → native :5432 fallback.
- Pin port across desktop restarts with `PAPERCUSP_PG_PORT=<port>` env.
- `paperclip` DB and marketplace stay on native :5432 (out of scope — user's call).
- Migration runner strips lines starting with `\` (psql metacommands aren't valid SQL); `040-plugin-configs-backfill.sql` is in `MANUAL_ONLY` skip list (needs `psql -v key=...`).
- `CREATE PUBLICATION zero_harness FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA harness_shared, papercup_shared` MUST run AFTER migrations (the schemas don't exist on fresh initdb until 001-shared.sql applies).
- `plpgsql.so` must NOT be stripped from embedded-pg bundle — earlier `pl*.so` sweep killed it; build script now scopes strip to `plperl/plpython/pltcl` only.

Related: [[no-regex-for-func-args]], [[pg-canonical-no-mirrors]].
entries.description: Embedded PG discovery file at ~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json — desktop writes port on boot, deletes on shutdown; webapp/agents resolve via getHarnessAdminUrl()

entries.text:
The operator `/harness` page opens ~6 long-lived SSE `EventSource`
streams (`/api/zero-harness/sse` — sometimes 2×, `/api/flags/stream`,
`/api/ui/intents/stream`, `/api/operator/state-snapshot`,
`/api/harness/:slug/log/stream`). Chromium allows only **6 connections
per origin** for HTTP/1.1, so on-demand `fetch()`s (e.g. the commit-diff
`git/show`) get zero free sockets and hang until timeout. The server is
fine — `curl` returns in ~1.5s. `HarnessZeroProvider.tsx` and
`app/harness/layout.tsx` already document this hazard in comments.

**Mitigation shipped 2026-05-20 (`c718d501`):** the commit-diff fetch is
routed cross-origin to the sibling loopback host (`localhost` ↔
`127.0.0.1`) via `apps/operator/lib/cross-origin-url.ts` — a distinct
origin gets its own fresh 6-socket pool. Hono's global CORS middleware
reflects the Origin so the cross-origin GET is allowed. This unblocks
the diff only.

**Real fix still open:** multiplex the operator SSE streams onto one
connection (`@restart/sse` has the channel primitives). Until then, any
new on-demand fetch on the harness page is at risk. Also seen: the
harness page intermittently self-reloads (kills in-flight fetches) —
uninvestigated. Related: [[feedback_webkitgtk_localhost_over_ip]] is the
libsoup/WebKit version of the same per-origin-pool problem.
entries.description: Operator /harness page opens ~6 SSE streams = the browser's whole HTTP/1.1 socket budget; on-demand fetches starve

entries.text:
As of 2026-05-07 the operator (apps/operator) no longer has a user-facing
login. Magic-link UI/routes deleted: `app/login`, `app/signup`,
`app/api/auth/login`, `app/api/auth/verify`. `lib/auth.ts` kept (other
features import `getSessionUser`); `/api/auth/{logout,status}` kept.

`/api/mobile/desktop/*` (mint-pair-token, list/revoke devices) gated by
`desktopAuth` → checks request `Host` header is in
{localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, [::1]}. Any other host = 403 loopback_only.
A synthetic `sessionUser={email:'local@desktop'}` is injected so
downstream code is unchanged.

Operator binds `127.0.0.1` by default in both `bin/prod` and
`apps/operator/package.json` dev/start scripts. Override via
`PAPERCUSP_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0` for LAN-device testing without `adb reverse`.

**Why:** magic-link auth was theatre — anyone who could reach :3070 could
self-issue a session by typing any email. Real protection is "only
loopback can connect" (OS-level via 127.0.0.1 bind) plus the Host header
gate as belt-and-suspenders. User wanted dev friction gone, accepted the
trade.

**How to apply:**
- Don't reintroduce session-cookie auth on `/desktop/*` routes — would
  break Quick-pair on localhost:1420 dev page.
- When operator gets exposed on Defguard mesh later, this needs a
  separate auth layer (mesh ACL, JWT, etc.) — Host check is spoofable.
- Phone-side endpoints (`/api/mobile/pair`, `/sync/sse`, etc.) are NOT
  affected — they use deviceAuth (JWT bearer), independent of desktopAuth.
- Emulator path: 10.0.2.2 maps to host's 127.0.0.1, works through
  loopback bind. Phone-side routes use deviceAuth so 10.0.2.2 Host is
  fine there. mint-pair-token is desktop-only (Host: localhost:1420 or
  :3055 or :3070 via Vite proxy / direct).
entries.description: Papercup operator pairing endpoints use Host-header loopback gate; magic-link UI removed; binds 127.0.0.1 by default

entries.text:
First-party tools that don't fit the plugin shape (operator scan,
voice config, harness phases, …) are exposed via D1a's
`defineTool({ requirePrincipal: false, roles, rolesQuota? })` flag.
Where the tool *file* lives depends on what code it imports:

**Package-side** — `packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/<group>/<verb>.ts`
- Use when the tool only needs `@restart/db-org` (PG), `zod`, and
  Node built-ins.
- Auto-loaded via the side-effect imports in
  `packages/agent-mcp/src/bootstrap.ts`.
- Example: `tools/artifacts/{load,save,append,delete}.ts` — pure PG.

**Operator-side** — `apps/operator/lib/agent-tools/<group>/<verb>.ts`
- Use when the tool depends on operator-app-only helpers (workspace
  registry, audit_log readers, scan-history libs, voice prefs, …)
  that the standalone agent-mcp package can't import (its
  `tsconfig.build.json` has `rootDir: ./src`).
- Each tool calls `defineTool({ ... })` from `@papercusp/agent-mcp`.
- Loaded via side-effect import:
  `apps/operator/lib/agent-tools/index.ts` lists each tool, and the
  catch-all route at
  `apps/operator/app/api/agent-tools/[...path]/route.ts` does
  `import '@/lib/agent-tools/index'` once near the top so the first
  request to /api/agent-tools/* triggers registration.
- Example: `lib/agent-tools/operator/{stats,last_scan,scans_list}.ts`.

**Why two locations:** packages-side tools survive future extraction
of agent-mcp as a standalone npm package; operator-side tools accept
the operator-app coupling in exchange for not duplicating ~500 lines
of operator-state SQL. Pick by what the tool needs, not by tier.

**Migration mechanics:** when wrapping a legacy
`/api/agent-mcp/<route>`, do NOT delete the legacy route in the same
PR if the operator UI still fetches it — the new tool surfaces the
same data via MCP, the legacy route stays for UI fetches until a
later cleanup pass switches the UI to POST against
`/api/agent-tools/<group>/<verb>`. Streaming routes (SSE / Claude
chat) stay legacy permanently per the brief's don't-migrate list.
entries.description: Where to put first-party (non-plugin) MCP tools — package-side vs operator-side, with the D1a defineTool flag

entries.text:
Papercusp's shipped product is a **desktop app backed by embedded
Postgres** (`embedded-postgres-server`, per-harness instance). The
Next.js webapp on `:3055`/`:3070` and the native PG on `:5432` are
**developer-convenience only**:
- webapp = nicer hot-reload than the desktop shell
- native PG = `psql` shell beats poking at embedded-pg from desktop
- desktop app currently points at native PG in dev for parity, will
  flip to embedded-pg before public release

**Why:** at public release we only support embedded-pg. Native PG
disappears. Webapp may stay as a dev tool but is not a shipped
artifact.

**How to apply:**
- New SQL migrations go in `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql`.
  Embedded-pg auto-applies via `migration-runner.js` (added 2026-05-05,
  tracks `harness_shared.schema_migrations`). Native PG still needs
  manual `psql -f` for dev — but the schema must work on embedded-pg
  because that's what ships.
- Don't add features that only run against system PG (cross-DB
  queries, OS-level pg tools, extensions embedded-pg doesn't have).
  If embedded-pg can't run it, it doesn't ship.
- Don't propose wiring a system-PG migration runner as a long-term
  fix — system PG is going away. It's a transient dev annoyance, not
  an architectural gap.
- Use the workspace-resolved PG connection, not hard-coded
  `localhost:5432`.

Documented in `papercup/CLAUDE.md` "Database topology" section and the
migration brief's traps table (updated 2026-05-10).

**Host-verify findings (2026-05-31), this dev box:** `:3070` is the
standing systemd `papercup-dev-api.service` (`npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts`,
logs `/tmp/dev-api.log`), NOT spawned by the desktop. No
`~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json` + no PG env URL → it uses the **native
fallback `postgresql://harness_admin:harness_admin_pwd@localhost:5432/papercusp`**
(native PG 18, alive — the CLAUDE.md "renamed to papercusp_legacy" note is
NOT true here). That native DB **drifts behind migrations** (was 8 behind
→ wave-advance sweep failed every tick). To apply pending: run
`applyPendingMigrations({client: postgres(DSN,{max:1}), sqlDir:
libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql})` from `embedded-postgres-server` (keys on
filename in `harness_shared.schema_migrations`; idempotent). Gotchas:
HTTP tool routes `POST /api/<group>:<verb>` are **gated → 404 to raw
curl** (need agent-session auth); the `mcp__papercusp-su__*` session is
partially-authed (`roles_known`/`plans:promote` preview work; `harness:list`
+ `/features/import` need bearer+workspace tx → "unknown project"). Restart
the host with `systemctl --user restart papercup-dev-api.service` (logs
`/tmp/dev-api.log`).

**Spawning agents from dev-api needs 3 env fixes the desktop sets but the
standing service didn't** (all added to `apps/operator/.env.local`, sourced
by ExecStart, gitignored; found 2026-05-31 verifying the promote role):
(1) `PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"` — service PATH lacks bun; omp's
`#!/usr/bin/env bun` shebang → `rc=127`. (2) `buildInvokeOnce` now sets
`PAPERCUSP_USE_PG_STATE=1` + `DATABASE_URL` (committed `2993f58`); without
them invoke/scoper/expert agents ran empty in-memory. (3)
`PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_URL=http://localhost:3070/api/mcp` — `spawn-mcp.ts`
defaults the agent's papercusp MCP server to `/api/sse` which **404s**; the
live agent-mcp endpoint is `/api/mcp` (streamable HTTP). Without it omp loads
**zero** papercusp tools. Even with all three, the spawned **agent no-ops** here for backend reasons
below the wave mechanism: **omp**'s default model `openai-codex/gpt-5.5`
(`~/.omp/agent/config.yml`) can't connect (codex websocket fails) → `rc=0`,
nothing. Switched to **claude-code** (`.env.local`: `AGENT_CMD="claude -p"` +
`AGENT_BACKEND="claude-code"`); claude-code WORKS in isolation with the exact
spawn flags (`--mcp-config <signed> --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode
bypassPermissions --include-partial-messages`), the `/api/mcp` config, harness
cwd, OAuth, and exact service env — but the orchestrator `invoke()` spawn
(`invoke.ts:1151`) captures ZERO stdout (no `<runId>.jsonl`); claude forks, the
parent returns in ~3.5s, an orphaned claude child runs ~20s. So the orchestrator's
claude-code spawn-mechanics path (rarely exercised; omp is default) is buggy —
instrument `invoke()` (log exact argv) to fix. The Anthropic *workspace* key is
fine — the earlier `401 invalid x-api-key` was a different (LLM-extraction) path.
entries.description: Public release ships desktop app on embedded-pg only; native PG :5432 + webapp are dev-only convenience; don't design around system-PG persistence

entries.text:
Verifying the `pui` (the ratatui terminal workbench, `apps/tui`, binary `pui`) live: drive a **FROZEN copy of the built release binary** in an **isolated PTY** (python `pty`+`pyte`) — never the user's terminal (no focus steal) and never a live-operator pui with spawn keys.

Harness lives at `/tmp/pui-livetest/` (`pui` frozen binary + `venv` with pyte + `drive.py`). Pattern: `pty.fork()` → child `execv` the binary with `TERM=xterm-256color` + `PAPERCUSP_TUI_OWNER=<test-owner>`; parent sets winsize via `TIOCSWINSZ`, pumps output into a `pyte.Screen`, sends keys with ~1s pauses, snapshots `screen.display`. Connects to the live operator over IPC (`~/.papercusp/endpoint-ipc.json`).

**Safe read-only keys** (autonomous OK): tab digits `1`-`0`, `f` Fleet, `o` Operator, `p` presence, `N` notifications, `?` help, `j/k`, `[`/`]`, `<`/`>`, `q`/Ctrl-C quit. **SPAWN keys — supervised only, NEVER autonomous** (they launch real agents / drive zellij): `n` (Sessions→psu agent), `Enter` (Plugins→plugin pane / Operator→composer), `i` (Operator composer), `g` (lazygit), palette `:` `:save-layout`/`:restore-crew`/`:restore-layout`. (Palette HTTP-only commands like `:pickup`/`:release` are safe autonomous against a throwaway plan.)

**⚠ STALE-trap (corrected 2026-06-05, su-af89a): bare `pui` no longer = HUD** — it auto-provisions a NEW zellij session (D-010) and runs `pui hud` inside it; a pyte drive of bare `pui` sees zellij chrome and your keys get eaten. **Drive `pui hud` directly** (the raw ratatui app in your pty). It creates throwaway zellij artifacts anyway — `zellij kill-session` your strays after. More gotchas: (a) this pyte build crashes on crossterm's private DSR queries — subclass `pyte.Screen` with no-op `report_device_status`/`report_device_attributes`; (b) wait ~8s + send Esc before the first `:` or boot repaint eats it and the letters leak as nav keys; (c) to point an isolated pui at staging :3170 instead of green :3070 IPC, set `HOME=<fake-home>` containing only `.papercusp/operator.json` `{"httpUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:3170","token":…}` (no endpoint-ipc.json → HTTP fallback); delete the fake home after (token copy). Worked example: /tmp/pui-livetest/drive_brief31.py.

2026-06-04 (su-ad289): first live interactive run — read path works across all 12 tabs; P-006 persistence restore verified live. 2026-06-05 (su-af89a, Brief 31): first live WRITE-path run — `:pickup`/`:release` toasts verified in the real TUI against :3170. See plan [[tui-workbench-ratatui-2026-06-04]]. Aligns with [[feedback_no_live_keystroke_drive_pui]] + [[feedback_own_xvfb_for_e2e]] (this is the terminal-app analogue).
entries.description: How to do a live interactive run/verification of the pui (apps/tui ratatui workbench) safely on the shared box

entries.text:
**Symptom:** a Restart shop data grid renders black/grey instead of blue-frost
(e.g. the 2026-05-30 `/wholesale` report).

**Cause:** papergrid (`@papercusp/token-kit` era — the `libs/papergrid` submodule)
was made **theme-agnostic** in the P4 design-token work: `GRID_COLORS`/`glideTheme`
ship a **brand-neutral dark default** (`#141414`-ish). Restart's frost palette only
applies once `configureGridColors(...)` runs — wired as a **side-effect import**
`import '../lib/grid-theme-init'` (apps/shop) that must be present in **every client
island that renders a grid**, before first render (the Glide canvas captures
`glideTheme` via `useMemo(()=>glideTheme,[])` at first render).

**The trap:** this includes BOTH papergrid grids (`GridTable`/`DataGridShell`) AND
`@restart/ui`'s `WholesaleProcurementGrid`/`WholesaleGlideGrid` (which also read
papergrid's `GRID_COLORS`/`glideTheme`). A grep for only papergrid components misses
the `@restart/ui` ones — which is how `WholesaleIsland` + `WholesaleGlideIsland` were
missed initially.

**Fix / check:** `grep -rlE '<WholesaleProcurementGrid|<WholesaleGlideGrid|DataGridShell|GridTable'
apps/shop/src` → every hit must also `grep grid-theme-init`. If not, add
`import '../lib/grid-theme-init';` at the top of that island.

**Better-fix-someday:** the per-island import is fragile (easy to miss one). A single
client bootstrap that runs `configureGridColors` before any grid mounts would remove
the whack-a-mole — but Astro has no single client entry, so per-island is the current
reliable pattern. Relates to [[feedback_visual_execution_weak_brief_for_designer]].
entries.description: Restart shop grids render BLACK if their island misses the grid-theme-init import — papergrid is brand-neutral by default; frost must be injected per-island

entries.text:
To reproduce Firefox-ONLY bugs in the Restart shop (e.g. the :4321 page-change
freeze), drive the user's **actual stock Firefox** — Playwright's bundled Firefox
and Chromium do NOT reproduce them.

**The snap-firefox + selenium recipe (this is the hard part):**
- User's `firefox` = snap build. `/usr/bin/firefox` and `/snap/bin/firefox` are
  WRAPPER SCRIPTS → geckodriver rejects them ("binary is not a Firefox executable").
- Use the REAL ELF + the snap's OWN bundled geckodriver:
  - binary: `/snap/firefox/current/usr/lib/firefox/firefox`
  - geckodriver: `/snap/firefox/current/usr/lib/firefox/geckodriver`
- Force geckodriver's temp profile into a HOME-accessible dir (snap can't read
  /tmp): run with `TMPDIR=/home/dev/.ff-tmp`.
- Isolated display so you never steal the user's :0 window: `Xvfb :99` +
  `DISPLAY=:99`. (Headed under Xvfb — real compositing matters for animation bugs.)
- selenium-webdriver installed in `/tmp/ffrepro/` (standalone, not the repo).
  Harness: `/tmp/ffrepro/repro.mjs` (loads `:4321/?sync=poll|ws`, triggers an Astro
  ClientRouter nav, then probes freeze via continuous rAF frame-gap monitor +
  click-responsiveness + asserts WS state via `window.__zero_instance_cache__` /
  `window.__SYNC_PROBE__`).

**Key finding (2026-06-01):** with the kvStore='mem' WS fix, BOTH poll and ws are
RESPONSIVE in clean Firefox 150.0.3 (max frame gap ~88ms). The harness uses a
FRESH profile — so a freeze the user still sees comes from ACCUMULATED profile
state (old IndexedDB Zero replica / cache / partytown SW) or a machine/GPU factor
Xvfb lacks, NOT from the shipped code. Disambiguate via the user's console:
`[...window.__zero_instance_cache__.keys()]` → a `…|idb` key = stale old bundle
(hard-reload fixes); `…|mem` = on the fix. See [[feedback_browser_e2e_verify_ui_fixes]].
entries.description: How to drive the user's REAL stock Firefox (snap 150.x) headlessly to reproduce Firefox-only shop bugs that Chromium/Playwright-Firefox can't

entries.text:
Restart storefront browser-e2e (`apps/shop/src/lib/**/*.e2e.test.ts`, playwright-core chromium-in-Vitest) **must target `http://localhost:4321`, never `127.0.0.1:4321`.**

**Why:** shop session cookies (`shop_cart_id`, better-auth `better-auth.session_token`) are set by shop-api on `localhost:3100` and are **host-scoped to `localhost`**. A page on `127.0.0.1:4321` is cross-site to `localhost:3100` → the browser silently drops those `SameSite=Lax` cookies → every request mints a fresh empty cart / anon session. Symptom: `POST /cart/items` returns 201 with items:1 but the next `GET /cart` returns items:0 (a NEW cart id each time, `cookie=` empty). The cart drawer correctly shows "empty"; looks like a persistence bug, is actually cookie host-scope.

**How to apply:** the `T0.6` harness (`apps/shop/src/lib/e2e/harness.ts`) default base URL is now `http://localhost:4321`; keep the `localhost` host if repointing `SHOP_BASE_URL` (e.g. post @astrojs/cloudflare cutover → workerd port). Documented in `apps/shop/TESTING.md`.

Other Phase-4 e2e gotchas (same harness): cart drawer is a Vaul portal that only mounts when open and does NOT reliably auto-open on add — open via `shop:cart-open` window event, poll-dispatched to beat CartShell's post-hydration listener; RegionPicker SSRs the default (US) label and only re-renders to the resolved region after hydration (assert currency €/$ or wait for the label); silktide consent injects a click-intercepting overlay — block it at the network layer (`route(/silktide/).abort()`). Stripe is test-mode (`pk_test_`/`sk_test_`) so the full guest purchase (card 4242 in the real PaymentElement) runs end-to-end. See [[project_restart_shop_preview_build]], [[project_restart_zerocache_inventory_collision]].
entries.description: Restart shop e2e MUST use localhost (not 127.0.0.1) or cart/auth cookies drop and every flow breaks

entries.text:
FIXED 2026-06-01. The Restart shop (:4321) freezing in Firefox on navigation was
NOT the React #418 (that fires under POLLING too and is recoverable) nor the
Zero WS client itself. **Root cause: zero-cache (:4848) was DOWN.**

Chain: zero-cache crash/stop leaves an orphaned `@rocicorp/zero/.../server/
replicator.js serving` worker holding the SQLite replica lock (`/tmp/
zero-replica.db`) → next start dies `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked:
journal_mode = delete` → :4848 stays down → the shop's WS probe to
ws://localhost:4848 fails (1.5-4s each), and it re-probed PER ISLAND × PER
ClientRouter navigation → the failing-probe churn freezes Firefox (Chromium
degrades gracefully, so it looked Firefox-only). Diagnose: `ss -ltn | grep 4848`,
`fuser /tmp/zero-replica.db` (find the orphan), the user's console shows
"Firefox can't establish a connection to ws://localhost:4848" repeating.

Manual heal: `fuser -k /tmp/zero-replica.db*` then
`overmind restart zero-cache -s .overmind-all.sock` (up in ~6s).

Two fixes shipped (local commits, not pushed):
- **libs/sync 4d32292** (`SyncProvider.tsx` `probeWebSocketOnce`): probe WS ONCE
  per session, cache the verdict on `window.__sync_ws_probe_cache__`; dead server
  detected once → graceful POLLING, no churn, no freeze. Verified in REAL stock
  Firefox 150 (see [[project_restart_real_firefox_repro_harness]]).
- **superproject fb3e06f1**: `bin/zero-cache-start.sh` auto-clears the stale
  replica lock (`fuser -k` scoped to ZERO_REPLICA_FILE, so it never touches the
  harness zero-cache :4849) before exec'ing zero-cache-dev; Procfile wired.
  ACTIVATED 2026-06-01 via full daemon restart (`overmind quit` +
  `bin/overmind-all start web zero-cache shop-api shop-app shop` — overmind caches
  the Procfile cmd at daemon start, so a plain `overmind restart <proc>` is NOT
  enough). Verified self-heal: stop→orphan→restart auto-recovers :4848 in ~12s,
  no manual kill. Shop (:4321) also re-integrated into overmind (no more setsid).
  Also 2026-06-01: same WS-probe-churn fix cut the :3001 admin Firefox-tab crash;
  trimmed eager git-graph.css (off root layout) + react-diff-view (lazy
  CommitDetail, git-graph 248f051) + BuildStatus fetch timeouts (superproject
  5265755a). And ENABLE_DEV_PASSWORD_RESET_VIEWER flipped 1→0 in .env (dev
  password-reset viewer was live; code was already env-gated/secure).

WS is the shop default (cart island passes syncType="WEBSOCKETS" in
Layout.astro). Earlier red herrings I burned time on: PageTransition,
rest-query-batch, WebSocketAdapter keep-alive, kvStore='mem' (kvStore='mem' shop
WS is still in place + fine, but was NOT the freeze cause). Lesson: when a shop
symptom is transport-specific, CHECK THE BACKEND IS UP first.
entries.description: Restart shop :4321 "freezes on page change in Firefox" — real root cause is a DOWN zero-cache (:4848), not React

entries.text:
The Restart storefront (`apps/shop`, port 4321) runs via **`astro preview`**, which serves the **built `dist/`** — NOT `astro dev`. A source edit (e.g. a `.tsx` island) is invisible until you `npm run build` in `apps/shop` AND restart the preview process (the node server loads the server bundle into memory at startup). Build ≈ 20s.

Verify a build picked up a change by grepping the client chunk:
`grep -rl "<marker>" apps/shop/dist/client/_astro/<Component>.*.js`.

**shop-api CORS allowlist is only `http://localhost:4321` and `:3002`** (`apps/shop-api/src/main.ts:50-52`, `SHOP_ORIGIN`/`SHOP_APP_ORIGIN`). So you CANNOT browser-test the shop on an ad-hoc port (e.g. 4399) — Zero `/zero/rest-query`, `/cart`, etc. get CORS-blocked. To test a fresh build, take over 4321 itself (overmind panes use `remain-on-exit on`, so killing the preview frees the port without a respawn fight).

Zero realtime is real here: `zero-cache` runs on **:4848** (`Procfile`, `.overmind.env`), WS probe connects in <10ms on localhost. `useSyncQuery` from `@restart/sync` + `products.byGroupIds` is the live path; `storefront_product` is the published mirror (`availableQty` is a GENERATED column = `GREATEST(0, qty - reservedQty)`).

DB for manual stock/price pokes: `psql postgresql://postgres_app:postgres@localhost:5432/restart`. Related: [[project_restart_stack]], [[reference_restart_repo]].

entries.text:
The user's primary project is "Restart" at `/home/dev/Restart`. Full stack is started with `bin/overmind-all start` from the project root.

**Port map:**
| Service | Port |
|---|---|
| web (Next.js admin) | 3001 |
| shop (Astro storefront) | 4321 |
| api-gateway (NestJS) | 3000 |
| shop-api (NestJS) | 3100 |
| browser-use | 3210 |
| code-server | 8082 |
| docs-viewer | 4325 |

**Conventions:**
- `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` always required
- Drizzle migrations: `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f drizzle/NNNN_*.sql` — NOT drizzle-kit migrate
- `owner-central-server/` submodule: OFF LIMITS — never modify

**Startup procedure:**
```bash
cd /home/dev/Restart
rm -f .overmind-all.sock   # remove stale socket first
bin/overmind-all start
```

**Stale socket trap:** Child processes from a previous session survive the lost parent and keep holding their ports. The new overmind will show those services as `dead` even though ports are bound. Before removing the socket: `pgrep -af overmind` and `ss -tlnp | grep -E '3001|4321|3000|3100'` to see what's still alive. Also check `ls /tmp/overmind-*` — multiple sockets means multiple ghost sessions.

**Overmind stale 'dead' status:** Processes restarted out-of-band keep old pid and show 'dead' in overmind status even when the port is listening. Cosmetic only. Confirm with user before `overmind restart` — it causes a brief service interruption.

**Admin tables empty (Approvals/Rejections):** Root cause is almost always the `gateway` overmind process (api-gateway :3000) being down. Admin at :3001 proxies all `/stats/*` to :3000; ECONNREFUSED silently leaves tables empty. Fix: `OVERMIND_SOCKET=.overmind-all.sock overmind restart gateway` from `/home/dev/Restart`.

**Why:** User repeatedly asks things like "start the Restart services" or "our app at :3001 is down" without specifying path or command — they expect you to know. The stale socket / ghost-process trap causes repeated confusion.

**How to apply:** When user refers to "the app," ":3001," or "Restart services" without a path, operate in `/home/dev/Restart`. Use `bin/overmind-all` for the full stack. For a single service: `OVERMIND_SOCKET=.overmind-all.sock overmind restart <name>`. Verify actual port binding with `ss -tlnp` before concluding a service is down.
entries.description: Location, startup command, ports, and recovery procedures for the Restart monorepo dev stack

entries.text:
Restart's single-node Typesense (Docker `typesense`, compose `docker-compose.typesense.yml`, project `restart`) silently took product search down from **2026-05-27 → 2026-05-28** (~36h, plus an earlier self-recovered episode 2026-04-23).

**Root cause (CONFIRMED — fd exhaustion, NOT transient I/O):** every Raft snapshot makes RocksDB hard-link all its `.sst` files; `storefront_products` has **~976 .sst files** and the process holds **~1000 fds while loaded**, against a container **nofile soft limit of 1024**. The snapshot exceeds 1024 → EMFILE → `Checkpoint creation failure, code 5` → SnapshotError → lone node steps down, can't `reset_peer` → "no leader" wedge. Recurs on EVERY snapshot. **Fix = `ulimits.nofile` soft 1024→524288** (host hard limit already 524288) in both compose files. NOT OOM (mem ~1.6G/16G), NOT disk-full (~60%), NOT mongod/CPU (I wrongly blamed mongod mid-session — it was fd all along), NOT OpenAI timeouts. `--reset-peers-on-error` + autoheal only recover the wedge after the fact; raising nofile removes the cause. Manual recovery if it ever recurs = `docker restart typesense` (reloads ~1M docs; watch `docker logs -f typesense | grep -i loaded`).

**Fix (commits on master ~2026-05-28):** `--reset-peers-on-error` (auto-recovers the wedge) + a `/health`-body healthcheck (over bash `/dev/tcp` — the `typesense/typesense:29.0` image has NO curl/wget but ships bash) + a `willfarrell/autoheal` sidecar (restart-on-unhealthy, since restart-on-exit never fires). Prod compose bumped `0.25.2 → 29.0` (0.25.2 predates the auto-embedding schema, so prod likely never built the collection and was permanently on the SQL fallback). Runbook: `docs/guides/typesense-outage-runbook.md`.

**GOTCHA (load-bearing):** the healthcheck `start_period` MUST exceed the cold reload (set to **3600s** after 900s proved too short). During reload `/health` is `{"ok":false}`; with a short start_period, autoheal marks it unhealthy and kills it mid-load → infinite restart loop that never finishes (observed live: a co-tenant `mongod` pinning ~15 cores stretched the ~12-min reload to ~20+ min and 900s let autoheal loop-kill it). A healthy node passes within seconds regardless, so a long start_period is free. NOTE: `docker restart` reuses the container's *baked-in* healthcheck config, NOT the compose file — to apply a changed `start_period` you must `docker compose up -d` (recreate), which re-triggers a reload. The running container now has 3600s + `--reset-peers-on-error` baked in.

**Write-path wedge (2026-05-28):** after the recovery, Typesense *reads/search were healthy but document WRITES hung* — a single upsert never returned and the indexer queue (`queued_writes`) wouldn't drain, while query-embedding + search worked fine. This blocks the catalog→Typesense sync pipeline, not just search. It was **transient post-recovery state**; a clean `docker compose up -d` restart cleared it and writes applied normally afterward. (Diagnosing it: test a write with `curl ...?action=upsert` + a timeout; exit 124 = wedged, 0 = healthy. Test container egress with **bash** `/dev/tcp`, never `sh`/dash — dash lacks `/dev/tcp` and gives false "no egress" negatives.)

While Typesense is down, search degrades to the Postgres FTS path — see [[project_restart_search_fts_fallback]].
entries.description: Restart Typesense single-node Raft wedge — root cause, fix flags, and the autoheal start_period gotcha

In the papercup superproject (`/home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup`), `libs/papercusp`, `libs/papercusp-shared`, `libs/sse`, etc. are **git submodules** (github.com/Papercusp/*). The commits the superproject **pins are local-only — never pushed to origin** (each submodule's `origin/main` is *behind* the pinned SHA). So the orchestrator/chat code (`invoke.ts`, `spawn-mcp.ts`, `chat-stream.ts`, …) lives in submodule repos, not the superproject.

**Why this bites:** a fresh `git worktree` on superproject `main` **cannot** `git submodule update --init` these — git tries to fetch the pinned SHA from origin and fails with `upload-pack: not our ref <sha>` / `did not contain <sha>`. The only checkout of the pinned code is whichever superproject checkout already has the submodules populated (normally the main shared dir).

**How to land a code change in a submodule and get it onto superproject main:**
1. Edit + verify (typecheck/tests) in the shared checkout's submodule working tree (e.g. `libs/papercusp/...`) — that's where node_modules/toolchain resolve.
2. `git -C libs/<sub>` commit on the submodule's **`main`** branch (it's usually checked out at the pinned SHA == submodule main tip; `papercusp` may show a detached `papercup-pin-*` tag but local `main` == pin).
3. In a superproject checkout that's on `main`, `git add libs/<sub>` (bumps the gitlink) and commit — pathspec-commit only your submodule(s) so others' dirty submodules don't ride along.
4. **Do NOT push to github.com/Papercusp** without being asked — superproject main already pins unpushed submodule commits, so pushing is a separate, batched step the team defers. "On main" here = local main + bumped pointer.

Plumbing note: `git update-index --cacheinfo 160000,<sha>,libs/<sub>` only works when the submodule path is already tracked in that worktree's index — it fails (`cannot add ... missing --add option`) in a worktree where the submodule was never initialized. Easier to bump the pointer from a checkout that has the submodule populated. See [[shared-libs-use-papercusp-scope]] and plan `claude-code-backend-restore-2026-05-30`.
entries.description: papercup submodule (libs/papercusp, libs/papercusp-shared) pinned commits are LOCAL-ONLY; how to land a code change in one and reach main

**Repo root:** `/home/dev/autonomous-harness/`
**Main driver:** `run.sh` — iteration loop; calls `ensure-docs.sh` at startup so every project has a docs tree before the documenter fires.
**Docs viewer launcher:** `bin/docs-viewer.sh` — symlinks each project's `docs/` into a Starlight app, calls `ensure-docs.sh` per project before mounting.
**Docs scaffolder:** `bin/ensure-docs.sh` — idempotent; creates `docs/{index.md, features/_placeholder.md, guides/_placeholder.md}` if missing.
**Project registry:** `~/.restart-harness-projects.json` — list of projects the harness knows about; adding a project here auto-scaffolds and auto-mounts on next docs-viewer restart.

**Scoper modes (as of 2026-04-25):**
- `MODE=initial` → reads SPEC.md → produces features.json + validation-contract.md
- `MODE=proposal` → reads harness state → writes `.harness/proposals/<ts>.md`
- `MODE=replan` → reads SPEC.md (post-accept, new bullets already appended) → preserves all existing feature `id`/`status`/`attempts` → appends new VAL-* + F-* entries → outputs `REPLANNED: +N features, +M assertions` or `REPLAN_NOOP`

**Full closed loop (wired 2026-04-25):**
```
scoper MODE=initial
  → SPEC.md → features.json + validation-contract.md
... harness runs features to DONE ...
scoper MODE=proposal → .harness/proposals/<ts>.md
review_pending_proposals
  → reviewer MODE=proposal (per file)
  → on ACCEPT: apply_proposal_to_spec (appends bullets to SPEC.md)
  → if any accepted + replanOnAccept=true: scoper MODE=replan
    → appends new F-*/VAL-* entries, preserves in-flight status
... main loop picks up new todos ...
```

**Config knobs:**
- `reviewer.replanOnAccept` (default `true`) — set `false` to keep auto-accept but skip replan
- `product.enabled` (existing) — disables upstream proposal generation entirely

Meridian's `mapModelToClaudeModel` (in `@rynfar/meridian` cli bundle) collapses the client's model string to a short alias before forwarding:
- Contains `"opus"` → `opus[1m]` (or `opus` for subagents / when extended context is unavailable)
- Contains `"haiku"` → `haiku`
- Else → `sonnet` (or `sonnet[1m]` if `MERIDIAN_SONNET_MODEL=sonnet[1m]`)

So `claude-opus-4-7`, plain `opus`, etc. all collapse to the same upstream alias. Anthropic resolves the alias to the current snapshot — `opus` → **`claude-opus-4-7`** as of 2026-05-12 (verified via `claude --model opus --print --output-format json 'reply ok'`, response `modelUsage.claude-opus-4-7`).

**How to verify which model is actually serving:** run a fresh `claude --model <X> --print --output-format json 'reply ok'` outside the session and read `modelUsage.<resolved-id>` from the JSON. The system prompt's self-declaration is not authoritative; the API response is.

Meridian listens on 127.0.0.1:3456. Telemetry at `GET /telemetry/summary?window=<ms>` shows `byModel` keyed by whatever string the client sent (pre-mapping), not the upstream resolution. `/v1/models` is also pre-mapping — ignore it for "what's actually serving."
entries.description: Meridian (claude-bridge) accepts any opus/sonnet/haiku model string and forwards as an alias; opus resolves to claude-opus-4-7 upstream

In the **claude CLI v2.1.162**, `claude -p --model claude-opus-4-8` (the explicit
model id) is **accepted but silently runs `claude-opus-4-7`** — the explicit
4.8 id is NOT honored. The **alias `--model opus` correctly resolves to
`claude-opus-4-8`** (the latest). The flag never errors either way, so a spawn
command that *says* `--model claude-opus-4-8` is NOT proof the agent ran 4.8.

**Verify the ACTUAL model from the session transcript**, not the spawn command:
`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session>.jsonl` → the `message.model` field on
assistant rows. (This bit me: a papercup merge-resolver spawned with
`--model claude-opus-4-8 --effort xhigh` actually ran opus-4-7; I'd "verified" 4.8
from the command string, which was wrong.)

**Fix / how to pin 4.8:** use the `opus` alias. For papercup per-role overrides,
`AGENT_MODELS` value `"opus:xhigh"` → `applyRoleModel` emits `--model opus --effort xhigh`
(see [[project_agent_launch_unification]]). The durable setting lives in the
operator AgentConfig (`POST /api/agent-config` → PG `operator_agent_config.models`
+ mirrored to `process.env.AGENT_MODELS`), kept in sync with `apps/operator/.env.local`.
`--effort` (low|medium|high|xhigh|max) DOES apply correctly.

**Remote-managed ingress (Cloudflare dashboard wins, local yml is ignored)** as of 2026-05-11 v13:

The mobile-pair endpoint `api.papercuspai.com/api/mobile/*` was 404 until 2026-05-11. Fix: added the path-specific rule above so mobile API traffic on the brand domain reaches the operator at :3070 (Hono), while marketplace traffic on the root path keeps going to :3057.

```sh
NEW_TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import json,base64,re; m=re.search(r'BEGIN ARGO TUNNEL TOKEN-----\n(.+?)\n-----END', open('/home/dev/.cloudflared/cert.pem').read(), re.DOTALL); print(json.loads(base64.b64decode(m.group(1).strip()+'==='))['apiToken'])")
ACCT=f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94
TUNNEL_ID=c53515b3-edfe-4e99-813b-e3916ae9d02c
# Fetch
curl -s "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCT/cfd_tunnel/$TUNNEL_ID/configurations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW_TOKEN" > /tmp/cf-config.json

curl -X PUT "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCT/cfd_tunnel/$TUNNEL_ID/configurations" \

```

Sweeping the papercup Tauri desktop (operator-vite SPA) for console errors: drive a DEDICATED instance on an isolated `DISPLAY=:101` via the `tauri-agent-tools` bridge (never the user's `:0` windows). Harness lived at `/tmp/e2e-driver.sh` + `/tmp/e2e-run.sh` (2026-06-02 session).

**The instrument MUST be:** idempotent install (single-wrap console via saved natives — guard `__E2E_HOOKED__`), NON-destructive reads (a destructive `drain` + the `ev` libsoup-retry = silent data loss → false negatives), explicit `reset`, and capture into an in-memory `window.__E2E__` array so SSE-heavy surfaces that wedge the bridge (e.g. `/pi`) can be read after escaping via client-side nav. Sweep via REALISTIC client-side nav from ONE fresh `/adv` bootstrap; the only hard-reload is to the stable `/adv` shell.

**3 false-signal classes that look like bugs but aren't (all ~40 surfaces are otherwise clean):**
1. `/harness/*` "Importing a module script failed" → "Something went wrong" boundary = STALE dynamic-import chunk after a `vite build --watch` rebuild under a long-lived page. By design (`ChunkReloadPrompt` shows a reload toast; deliberately not suppressed). Clean on fresh page. Render-gate `kids>0` + re-bootstrap to confirm.
2. Transient `Load failed` / `replaceState`→`v` nav-abort `unhandledrejection` on `/adv/*` tabs = libsoup ~6-conn pool flap / superseded-navigation race under rapid sweeping. Non-deterministic, ~1 per full sweep, never reproduces in isolation.
3. `[TAURI] Couldn't find callback id N` flood = RELOAD-orphaned IPC streams (was real, see below).

**The one real bug found + FIXED (2026-06-02):** visiting `/pi` (terminal) or any reload while app-shell SSE-over-IPC streams are open orphaned Tauri `Channel` callbacks — Rust kept emitting to dead callback ids FOREVER (flood, ~21 warns/5s idle even on `/adv`). Root: `endpoint_ipc.rs` `channel.send().is_ok()` returns Ok even when the JS callback is gone (webview logs the warn, not Rust) + no on-reload cancel. NORMAL client-side nav cleans up fine (`close()`→`endpoint_cancel`); only RELOAD leaks. Fixed by another agent via D-012 (IPC bridge, `main.rs`). Verified flood 56→0, idle 21/5s→0. See [[feedback_webapp_retired_use_tauri_dev]], [[project_harness_sse_pool_exhaustion]].

On the standing dev box, `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` runs
`bin/desktop-dev-nohmr`, which launches `tauri dev` with `devUrl` overridden to
**:3070** (you'll see the running proc as `npm run tauri dev --config {"build":{"devUrl":"http://localhost:3070"}}`).
The :3070 Hono host serves the **BUILT** `apps/operator-vite/dist/`, kept fresh by
a `vite build --watch`. So the desktop webview is **NOT** the :3055 HMR dev server.

Consequences for verifying an operator-vite (SPA) change in the desktop:
- A source edit reaches the webview only after the `vite build --watch` rebuilds
  `dist/` (a few seconds) **and** the webview is reloaded (Ctrl+R) — there is **no
  live HMR** in the desktop. (`:3055` HMR still exists and compiles, but the
  desktop doesn't load it.) If a fresh webview load shows
  *"operator-vite is not built…"* you caught it mid-rebuild — reload after the
  watch finishes.
- A `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` change (e.g. `dragDropEnabled`)
  is a Rust/window-config change: it needs a **binary recompile + window restart**,
  which the running `tauri dev` does automatically when it sees the file change
  (fast incremental relink). A webview reload alone does NOT apply it.

Isolated-instance gotcha (for [[feedback_own_xvfb_for_e2e]] /
[[feedback_drive_desktop_with_tauri_agent_tools]]): a 2nd `tauri dev` under Xvfb
safely **reuses** the running backend (beforeDevCommand `dev-operator-ifneeded.sh`
skips the spawn when :3055 is bound; dev mode skips the sidecar). Its
tauri-agent-tools bridge port is auto-assigned (read the real port/token from
`/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token`; `--port/--token` go on the **subcommand**,
e.g. `eval --port …`). BUT bridge-eval `fetch`es to authed operator endpoints
return **403** in the 2nd instance (no authed session/workspace) — so
data-dependent UI (e.g. `plans:list` → the PlanRail rows) won't load there. Good
for routing/render checks (the route resolves, the component mounts); not for
data-driven UI. Verify data-driven UI with a unit test or in the user's authed
window instead.
entries.description: papercusp-desktop `npm run dev` = desktop-dev-nohmr → webview loads BUILT dist on :3070 (no HMR); how SPA vs Tauri-config changes deploy + the isolated-instance 403

## Where the build flow lives

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `setup-signing-key.sh` | One-time: generates the Tauri updater minisign keypair into `~/.papercusp/signing/` and updates `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`'s `pubkey` to match |
| `release-local.sh <version> <channel>` | Bumps versions → builds the sidecar (`papercup/apps/operator` → `src-tauri/sidecar/`) → `tauri build` (signed) → generates `latest.json` → commits + tags + pushes → `gh release create/upload` |
| `setup-posthog.sh` | Interactive `~/.papercusp/posthog.json` setup for admins enabling PostHog feature flags + telemetry forwarding |

Documentation: `papercusp-desktop/SHIPPING.md` (rewritten 2026-05-13 for the local flow).

## Build targets supported

| Target | Default | How to enable |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 | ✓ always | — |
| Linux arm64 | optional | `WITH_ARM64=1 bin/release-local.sh …` |
| Windows x86_64 | optional | `WITH_WINDOWS=1 bin/release-local.sh …` |
| macOS universal | ✗ | requires real Mac hardware + Apple Developer cert; not buildable from Linux |

## What this means for agent behavior

- **Never suggest creating `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`** or anything that does CI desktop builds. The decision is local-only.
- **Never suggest setting `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` or `SIBLING_REPO_PAT` as GitHub Actions secrets.** Both are local: `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` is read from `~/.papercusp/signing/papercusp.key` by `release-local.sh`; no sibling-repo PAT is needed since cross-repo clones aren't happening in CI.
- **Test workflows are still allowed.** `papercup/.github/workflows/{test,test-nightly,audit-harness-fs,labeler}.yml` are NOT covered by this — they're PR validation, not builds. Only the *desktop release* pipeline is legacy.
- If the user asks "why did the build fail" or "where's the release manifest", the right answer points at `bin/release-local.sh` and `gh release view`, NOT `gh run view`.

Related: [[reference_claude_bridge_models]] (independent), the V1 PostHog architecture lives at <https://docs.papercupai.com/posthog>.

In a **dev** Tauri instance (`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`), `installDesktopIpcPolyfills`
monkey-patches `window.fetch` → `ipcFetch` (sys:http over the endpoint-IPC socket).
The Rust side resolves the socket by re-reading **`~/.papercusp/endpoint-ipc.json`**
on every (re)connect — on the dev box that file is published by the **GREEN release
operator (`:3070`, papercup-release)**. So the webview's `/api/*` calls do **NOT**
go to the `devUrl` origin: even with `devUrl` pointed at staging `:3170`, API
responses come from green. Symptom: a brand-new main-only route works via `curl
:3170/...` but returns green's `{"error":"not_found"}` (the endpoint-route
`method-not-allowed.ts` notFound hook) inside the webview.

How to live-verify a new route + its UI pre-promotion (worked 2026-06-05, Brief 7):
1. `vite build` in `apps/operator-vite` (no watch may be running), confirm
   `:3170/<route>` serves the SPA (a 503 means mid-rebuild — retry).
2. Isolated instance: `DISPLAY=:97 PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT=<port> vglrun -d egl0
   npm run tauri -- dev --config '{"build":{"devUrl":"http://localhost:3170","beforeDevCommand":""}}'`
   (`beforeDevCommand:""` is REQUIRED post-cutover — the default
   `dev-operator-ifneeded.sh` would try to boot the integration stack onto :3070
   and collide with the green service). Real bridge port/token come from
   `/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token`, not the env var.
3. UI render path: assert tabs/sections mount via `tauri-agent-tools eval`; for
   data rows, stub `window.fetch` for the one endpoint in-page and remount via SPA
   tab clicks (no reload, keeps the stub) — full real-WebKitGTK render w/o the
   topology fight. API behavior itself: `curl :3170` after
   `systemctl --user restart papercup-staging-api`.
4. `PAPERCUSP_CUSTOM_PROTOCOL_UPSTREAM` only overrides the custom-protocol
   (`papercusp://`) forwarder, NOT the endpoint-IPC target — don't bother for this.

Related: [[reference-desktop-dev-nohmr-3070-dist]] (content source),
[[reference_3070_host_papercup_release]] (two-port model),
[[feedback_own_xvfb_for_e2e]] (isolation discipline).

In Restart's `@restart/db` (drizzle-orm `postgres-js` driver), interpolating a JS array into a raw `sql\`\`` template renders it as a **parenthesized placeholder list** `($1, $2, ...)`, NOT a single array param.

Consequence:
- ❌ `WHERE col = ANY(${scopes})` → renders `ANY(($1,$2))` → **invalid** (ANY needs an array, got a tuple) → query throws.
- ✅ `WHERE col IN ${scopes}` → renders `IN ($1,$2)` → valid IN-list.

This bit Scout's pgvector memory recall (2026-05-29): recall used `= ANY`, silently threw, the degrade-safe path swallowed it to `[]`, and the LLM *masked* the failure by parroting the `remember` tool's description examples as if they were real memories — so it looked like memory worked. Fixed by switching to `scope IN ${scopes}` in `apps/scout-service/src/memory/memory.service.ts`.

**How to apply:** for a scope/id filter against a raw `sql\`\`` query, use `IN ${array}` (drizzle adds the parens — don't add your own). If you genuinely need `ANY` (e.g. pgvector ops, array overlap), build a real array literal/param, not array interpolation. Lesson 2: a degrade-safe catch can hide a hard bug — log the failure (we added a recall-count debug line) and don't trust "it works" when an LLM could be hallucinating the success. See [[feedback_search_web_before_15_loops]].
entries.description: drizzle+postgres-js renders an interpolated JS array as `($1,$2)`, so `= ANY(${arr})` breaks but `IN ${arr}` works

entries.text:
**Symptom:** an operator route/tool 500s (or a module fails to load) with
`The requested module 'pkg' does not provide an export named 'X'`. Happens when an
**ESM** file (`"type":"module"` package, e.g. `@papercusp/operator-core`) does
`import { X } from 'cjs-pkg'` and runs under **tsx** (the `:3070` host —
`npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts`). tsx transpiles a **typeless** package's `.ts` to CJS;
Node then statically links the named import via `cjs-module-lexer`, which can't see
`export *` re-export chains or some packages' compiled named exports → the namespace
links EMPTY → every named import throws.

**Why it hides:** vitest/vite **bundle** (cross-module analysis, no lexer), so unit
tests + typecheck pass. Only the tsx runtime hits it, and route handlers lazy-load,
so "tests pass / host boots 200" masks broken routes.

**Fix:**
- **Our typeless `@papercusp/*` dep** → add `"type":"module"` to its package.json so
  tsx emits native ESM re-exports. ESM-ify any CJS-isms: `require()`→
  `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, `__dirname`→`import.meta.dirname`.
- **Third-party CJS you can't flip** (`@xterm/headless`, `cron-parser`, `yaml`,
  `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, …) → use a **static or dynamic import, NOT createRequire**.
  createRequire works under tsx but BREAKS the desktop sidecar esbuild bundle
  (`papercusp-desktop/bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh`, `--format=esm`, inlines all
  non-native deps): esbuild only inlines the GLOBAL `require('literal')`, so a renamed
  `nodeRequire(...)` stays a runtime call → "Cannot find module" in the shipped
  sidecar. Pick by namespace shape (probe with `import * as ns`): symbol on `ns` →
  `import * as ns from 'pkg'; ns.Sym`; only on `ns.default` → `import def from 'pkg';
  def.Sym`; lazy/optional dep inside an async fn → `await import('pkg')`. `const X =
  ns.Sym` keeps both value use + `InstanceType<typeof X>` type use. createRequire is
  fine ONLY for node builtins (`node:fs`/`node:os` — runtime-resolvable in the bundle).

**Find every break:** load each route+tool module under tsx and catch "does not
provide an export". Namespace-import probes give false +/- (tsx elides type-only
imports; a CJS runtime namespace can carry a key the static lexer can't, e.g.
`@xterm/headless` `Terminal`). Verify bundle-safety by esbuild-bundling each changed
file standalone and confirming the dep is inlined. Restart `:3070` after edits
(no hot-reload). Related: [[feedback_webapp_retired_use_tauri_dev]].
entries.description: Fix for "does not provide an export named X" when an ESM (type:module) papercup package named-imports a CJS dep under tsx — and the bundle-safe pattern that also survives the desktop sidecar esbuild build

entries.text:
git-sync (the papercup shared-tree auto-commit routine) escalates merge
**conflicts** to merge-resolver, but push **errors** only land in
`harness_shared.routines.metadata` (`WHERE name='git-sync'` → `last_error`,
`last_status`) — no coord broadcast, no journal lines. If `main` is N commits
ahead of origin with a clean tree, read that metadata first
(EI-18 tracks adding real escalation).

Gotchas learned 2026-06-05 (20h silent wedge, 67 commits / 10.4GB ahead):
- `git push --dry-run` SUCCEEDING proves nothing — dry-run never sends the
  pack. The real failure was GitHub HTTP 500 "unexpected disconnect while
  reading sideband packet" = oversized pack / >100MB blobs (GitHub hard limit;
  such a range can NEVER self-heal).
- Usual root cause: `add -A` sweeping un-ignored build artifacts (3rd time it
  was Rust `target/` — now covered by `apps/*/target/` in .gitignore).
- Recovery recipe (verified): pause routine (`UPDATE harness_shared.routines
  SET active=false WHERE name='git-sync'`) → safety branch → fix .gitignore →
  `git reset --soft origin/main` (working tree untouched; peers unaffected) →
  `git rm -r -f --cached <artifact dirs>` → one collapse commit → push →
  verify content-identity vs safety branch (`git diff --stat <safety> main --
  . ':(exclude)<dirs>'` should show only .gitignore) → delete safety branch,
  reactivate routine, background `git gc --prune=1.hour.ago`.
- `cat-file --batch-check` parsing trap: a format WITHOUT `%(rest)` makes
  cat-file treat the whole `sha path` line as the object name → everything
  "missing" → silently 0 results. Include `%(rest)` when piping from
  `rev-list --objects`.

Related: [[git-sync-live]], [[feedback_never_git_stash_shared_tree]]
entries.description: git-sync push failures are SILENT — diagnose via harness_shared.routines metadata (name='git-sync', last_error); oversized-blob wedge recovery = pause routine, ignore+untrack, reset --soft origin/main, collapse, push

Testing real mic-capture / speaker-playback code (cpal/rodio) on this box without
emitting real sound or touching the Brio / HDMI defaults (the audio analog of
[[own-xvfb-for-e2e]] / [[e2e-no-focus-steal]]):

1. Create an isolated sink + monitor source:
   `pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=pui_voice_test sink_properties=device.description=pui_voice_test`
   → gives output `pui_voice_test` + input `pui_voice_test.monitor`. Unload with `pactl unload-module <id>` after.
2. cpal's ALSA host exposes a **`pulse`** device (both in + out) that bridges to
   PipeWire's pulse layer, which **honors `PULSE_SINK`/`PULSE_SOURCE` env vars**
   (per-process, NO change to system defaults).
3. Route the test process: `PULSE_SINK=pui_voice_test PULSE_SOURCE=pui_voice_test.monitor`
   and target the cpal device named `pulse` (substring match). Playback lands in
   the null sink; capture reads its monitor → a real loopback with zero audible sound.

Gotchas: the pulse bridge captures at 44100 Hz (resample as needed). A naive
zero-crossing frequency estimate over a buffer with trailing silence reads LOW
(measured 440·tone_len/window) — make the played tone longer than the capture
window and analyze the middle 60%.

Used to verify Brief 16's `apps/tui/src/voice.rs` (record/play/440Hz-loopback
smokes) — see [[webapp-retired-use-tauri-dev]] for the surrounding TUI context.
entries.description: For isolated audio capture/playback e2e on this PipeWire box, use a module-null-sink + cpal's `pulse` device with PULSE_SINK/PULSE_SOURCE — zero real sound, no focus steal

When driving an **isolated** operator Tauri desktop for e2e (own Xvfb + VirtualGL,
launched via `papercusp-desktop` `npm run dev` = `desktop-dev-nohmr`, devUrl `:3070`),
the webview's `fetch('/api/...')` goes **directly over HTTP to :3070** — it does NOT
ride the IPC bridge that the *real* desktop uses. The real desktop's IPC bridge injects
the operator superuser bearer on the upstream hop (`endpoint-ipc/server.ts`
`sysHttpInjectHeaders` → `principalFromSuperuserToken` → `trust:'trusted'`), which clears
admin gates. The isolated instance presents as `unverified-loopback`, so admin routes
(e.g. `/api/admin/llm-tests/*`) return **403 `trust unverified-loopback not in allowlist`**.

To reproduce the authorized path, monkeypatch `window.fetch` via the tauri bridge to add
`Authorization: Bearer <~/.papercusp/superuser-token>` for `/api/*`. **Gotcha:** the patch
MUST handle `URL` objects — panels call `fetch(new URL(endpoint, origin))`, and a `URL` is
neither a string nor a `Request`, so a naive `input.url` read misses it (read `input.href`
for URL). The patch survives client-side SPA nav (TanStack Router) but is lost on full
reload — remount the panel by clicking tabs, not `location.reload()`.

Bridge reads the DOM even GL-less, so DOM assertions are the authoritative proof; the
VirtualGL screenshot is only for literal pixel-paint. See [[own-xvfb-for-e2e]],
[[reference-desktop-dev-nohmr-3070-dist]], [[drive-desktop-with-tauri-agent-tools]].
entries.description: An isolated nohmr Tauri desktop's webview fetches :3070 /api DIRECTLY (not via the IPC bridge), so admin routes 403 "unverified-loopback" — inject the su bearer in-webview to reproduce the authorized path

# Kopia backup setup (configured 2026-05-10)

## Repo
- Path: `/mnt/data/Backup/kopia-repo` (4.5 TB free on /mnt/data)
- Password: `~/.config/kopia/password` (mode 600); also in 1Password
- `enableActions: true` set directly in `~/.config/kopia/repository.config` (no CLI flag)

## Sources (13)
All in `$HOME` unless noted:
owner-central-server, owner-Libs, papercup (stub, 20K), papercupai-workspace, papercup-public-site, papercusp-archive, papercusp-projects, Restart, .papercusp, .papercusp-workspaces, .ssh, .restart-harness-projects.json, /mnt/data/Backup/db-dumps

## Cadence + retention
- systemd user timer `kopia-snapshots.timer` every 5 min (`OnUnitActiveSec=5min`)
- Wrapper: `~/.config/kopia/snapshot-all.sh` runs hook once, then iterates sources
- Global policy: keep-latest 200, keep-hourly 48, keep-daily 30, keep-weekly 12, keep-monthly 12

## Pre-snapshot hook
`~/.config/kopia/hooks/pre-snapshot.sh` — runs ONCE per timer cycle (NOT via kopia's before-snapshot-root policy, that fires per-source). Dumps:
- PG 5432 → `/mnt/data/Backup/db-dumps/pg-5432.sql.gz` via `sudo -n -u postgres pg_dumpall` (peer auth)
- SQLite `models.db`, `agent.db`, `history.db` from Restart/.harness/pi-sessions/

## Deliberately skipped
- PG 16534 (papercusp embedded-pg): auth=password, no creds; file-level capture via `.papercusp-workspaces` source instead — relies on WAL replay
- Zero `replica.db`: custom format on top of sqlite, `.backup` fails "file is not a database"
- Docker volumes (bytebot-1/2-postgres on 5433/5434 = unrelated app, user excluded)

## Healthcheck
- `~/.config/kopia/healthcheck.sh` — alerts via `notify-send` if last snapshot >30min old
- Timer `kopia-healthcheck.timer` every 15min

## Ignores (global policy)
node_modules, .next, out, target, dist, build, .turbo, .cache, .svelte-kit, .nuxt, .angular, .vite, .parcel-cache, .yarn/cache, .pnpm-store, .bun, coverage, .nyc_output, __pycache__, *.pyc, .venv, venv, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .gradle, .terraform, tmp, .tmp, *.swp, *.swo, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, proc-macro-srv*, *.log

## Storage so far
~128 GB raw sources → 5.6 GB repo (4% storage cost). Per-cycle delta is KB-to-MB.

## Logs
- `~/.cache/kopia/snapshot-all.log` — per-cycle run output
- `/mnt/data/Backup/db-dumps/hook.log` — hook results
- `~/.cache/kopia/healthcheck.log` — healthcheck results

## Operations
- Live status: `systemctl --user list-timers kopia-snapshots.timer kopia-healthcheck.timer`
- Force snapshot: `~/.config/kopia/snapshot-all.sh` (synchronous, ~60s)
- Browse: `kopia snapshot list --all`
- Mount for restore: `kopia mount all /mnt/kopia-mnt`
- Repo size: `kopia content stats` or `du -sh /mnt/data/Backup/kopia-repo`

## Known fragility
- If user logs out without linger, timer stops. Linger=yes is set, but verify after major OS upgrades.
- `kopia snapshot list --all` parsing in snapshot-all.sh depends on output format — could break across kopia major versions

entries.text:
For a freeze-proof, layout-safe page/route transition in `motion/react`@12,
**animate opacity ONLY**. Three options, all verified against motion@12 in a
headless browser (verdict + `getAnimations()`):

1. **`y` / `x` / `scale` shorthand → MAIN THREAD.** Motion writes
   `style.transform` per frame (`getAnimations()` shows only opacity; inline
   transform churns e.g. `translateY(3.25px)`). The slide **freezes** whenever
   the main thread is blocked (heavy route mount). This was the original bug.
2. **Raw `transform: 'translateY(8px)'→'translateY(0px)'` string → WAAPI but
   BREAKS LAYOUT.** It runs on the compositor (`getAnimations()` shows two
   running animations, no inline churn), BUT Motion leaves `translateY(0px)` on
   the element at rest — computed transform = `matrix(…)`, not `none`. A
   non-none transform creates a **containing block** that reparents every
   `position: fixed` descendant. On pages with fixed layout (Restart's
   `FullBleedShell`) the fixed content visibly shifts (measured: a fixed child
   jumped `left: 0 → 208px`). The `y` shorthand avoids this (Motion cleans it to
   `none` at rest) — but it freezes (see #1).
3. **opacity-only → WAAPI + no transform at rest.** Opacity is always
   accelerated onto the compositor AND does not create a containing block. The
   only form that is both freeze-proof and layout-safe. Cost: no slide (pure
   cross-fade).

Also: `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` serializes exit→mount→enter, parking a heavy
mount in a blank/frozen gap — use an enter-only keyed `motion.div` instead.

Fixed the Restart `web` page-change freeze:
`apps/web/components/PageTransition.tsx` (opacity-only, enter-only). Verify any
change with verdict: `document.getAnimations()` (compositor handoff) AND
`getComputedStyle(el).transform` at rest (must be `none`). Related:
[[feedback_browser_e2e_verify_ui_fixes]].
entries.description: motion@12 transition gotchas — y shorthand = main-thread freeze; raw transform string = WAAPI but leaves a containing block; opacity-only is the safe one

OMP (Oh My Pi, `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`) ships these built-in tools natively. Source of truth: `~/.bun/install/cache/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent@<ver>/src/prompts/tools/*.md`.

## Built-in tool registry
`ask`, `bash`, `python`, `calc`, `ssh`, `edit`, `find`, `grep`, `ast_grep`, `ast_edit`, `lsp`, `notebook`, `read`, `browser` (puppeteer), `task`, `poll`, `todo_write`, `fetch`, `web_search`, `write`, `generate_image`.

## `lsp` operations (14)
`diagnostics`, `definition`, `type_definition`, `implementation`, `references` (3-line context for first 50), `hover`, `symbols` (file or workspace), `rename` (cross-codebase), `rename_file` (sends `workspace/willRenameFiles`), `code_actions` (list + apply), `status`, `capabilities` (per-server discovery), **`request` (raw LSP method — escape hatch)**, `reload`.

The `request` action means OMP-LSP is strictly more capable than any LSP-MCP wrapper for server-specific methods like `rust-analyzer/expandMacro`, `typescript/goToSourceDefinition`, `workspace/executeCommand`.

OMP's prompt enforces tool choice: "MUST use `lsp` for symbol-aware operations… MUST NOT perform cross-file renames with `ast_edit`/`sed`/manual edits when `lsp rename` works."

## `ast_grep` and `ast_edit`
Native bindings via `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` (Rust). Full metavariable matching (`$NAME`, `$_`, `$$$NAME`), language-specific guidance baked into the prompt. Languages: Python, JS/TS, Go, Java, C/C++, Rust, Ruby, PHP, more.

## What OMP does NOT have (real headroom)
- **Code graph / impact analysis** — no transitive call-chain or cluster reasoning. (GitNexus / CodeGraphContext fill this.)
- **Bulk repo packing** — no "pack the whole project as one document" tool. (Repomix fills this.)
- **Diff-aware prompts** — no "give me everything that changed since main" packer. (Code2Prompt fills this.)
- **Fast HTML→Markdown for web research** — `fetch` returns raw content; no Firecrawl/Jina-style cleaning layer.

## What is REDUNDANT to add as MCP
Don't ship MCP versions of: ast-grep-mcp, mcp-language-server, swiftlens, javalens-mcp, lsp-mcp-server, comby (for ast-grep-supported languages), Serena (capability-equivalent; only ergonomic gain). All are subsets or duplicates of OMP-LSP or OMP-`ast_grep`.
entries.description: Authoritative list of OMP's built-in tools and the lsp/ast-grep/ast-edit operation contracts; use to avoid recommending redundant MCPs

The operator API on `:3070` (the host `psu` and all `papercusp-su` MCP tools
talk to) runs as a **transient `systemd --user` unit** named
`papercup-dev-api.service`. Its ExecStart is
`bash -c "set -a; [ -f .env.local ] && . ./.env.local; set +a; exec npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts"`.

The relative paths (`.env.local`, `bin/hono-host.ts`) only resolve when the
unit's **WorkingDirectory = `…/papercup/apps/operator`** — the entry point is
`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts`, NOT `bin/hono-host.ts` at the repo root.

Failure mode seen 2026-06-05: the unit got (re)created with cwd = repo root, so
every start died instantly with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `bin/hono-host.ts` →
`status=1/FAILURE` → `Restart=always` crash-loop (counter hit 130+). `:3070` was
down during each gap, so `psu` printed
`psu: could not reach the operator at http://localhost:3070 (fetch failed)`.

Diagnosis path: `systemctl --user status papercup-dev-api.service` (climbing
restart counter = crash loop) → reproduce by running the ExecStart manually to
see the real error (journald only shows the systemd-level exit, not the app
stack trace). Booting from `apps/operator` works:
`[hono-host] listening on http://0.0.0.0:3070`.

Restore (also pins cwd so a future restart can't reintroduce the bug):
```
systemd-run --user --unit=papercup-dev-api.service \
  --working-directory=/home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup/apps/operator \
  -p Restart=always -p RestartSec=5 --setenv=PATH="$PATH" \
  /usr/bin/bash -c 'set -a; [ -f .env.local ] && . ./.env.local; set +a; exec npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts'
```
Nothing in the repo creates this unit (only `systemctl --user restart …` and the
`dev:restart` tool, which assume it already exists). Benign noise on boot that is
NOT the crash cause: `[ensure-omp-su] phase1 bootstrap failed: __dirname is not
defined` and `[boot-migrate] FAILED 000-baseline.sql: must be owner of function
task_lineage` — the host listens fine regardless. See
[[webapp-retired-use-tauri-dev]], [[verify-server-pid-before-measuring]].
entries.description: papercup-dev-api.service (the :3070 Hono operator) is a transient systemd --user unit that MUST run from apps/operator; wrong cwd → crash-loop → psu "fetch failed"

The mobile app is **`papercup-rust-mobile`** (`~/papercupai-workspace/papercup-rust-mobile/`):
one shared Rust core (`crates/papercup-core` + `crates/papercup-bindings` UniFFI) + native
Compose Android (`android/`) + SwiftUI iOS (`ios/`). Separate repo, **normal git commit/push**
(NOT git-sync managed).

**Android build/test on the dev box:**
- Regenerate Kotlin bindings after any UDL change: `make bindings-kotlin` (cargo uniffi-bindgen → `android/app/src/main/kotlin/uniffi/papercup/papercup.kt`).
- Full build: `tools/build-scripts/build-android.sh` = cargo-ndk cross-compile 4 ABIs (release) → `android/app/src/main/jniLibs/*/libpapercup.so` (gitignored) + `gradle assembleDebug` → `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. NDK at `~/Android/Sdk/ndk/27.0.12077973` (set `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`).
- Fast compile gate: `cd android && ./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin`.
- **On-device E2E IS possible on this box** (proven 2026-06-05): AVD `papercusp-test` (android-34 **google_apis** x86_64 — FCM works, real tokens mint), KVM present. Boot headless: `emulator -avd papercusp-test -no-window -no-audio -no-boot-anim -no-snapshot -wipe-data -gpu swiftshader_indirect` (no focus-steal). Pair against staging: mint a pair token on the host (`:3170` loopback), paste-payload in-app with `server=http://10.0.2.2:3170` via `adb shell input text` (compact JSON, single-quoted for the device shell). Drive via `uiautomator dump` bounds + `input tap`; screenshots `adb exec-out screencap -p`. Deep-link tests need the notification's flags: `am start --activity-single-top --activity-clear-top --ez/--es …` (without them `onNewIntent` never fires — looks like an app bug but isn't). `google-services.json` is in the build; `picovoice.access-key` absent → wake-word dormant. Kill with `adb emu kill`.
- **FCM push SEND works end-to-end** (verified 2026-06-05): the service-account key lives at `~/.papercusp/firebase-admin.json` (project `papercusp-mobile`), `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH` already in `apps/operator/.env.local`; the server's `device-push-credentials.ts` refresher mints OAuth tokens hourly. Gotcha: `dbosTimersActive()` must include the `PAPERCUSP_DBOS_ENABLE=1` launch gate or the refresher silently stands down on non-DBOS hosts (fixed in dbos-flags.ts; `[push-creds] FCM token refreshed` in the host journal = healthy). APNs (iOS) still needs the owner's `.p8` + Key ID + Team ID (`APNS_KEY_PATH`/`APNS_KEY_ID`/`APNS_TEAM_ID`). Headless-emulator GmsCore can wedge the FCM token fetch after a non-wiped cold boot — `-wipe-data` + re-pair fixes it; the startup registration is logged under `PapercupPush`.
- pre-push hook runs `make check` (Rust fmt-check + clippy -D warnings + cargo test) — must pass.

**Shared-checkout hazard:** the Android + iOS platform agents work the SAME working tree. A
`git add -A` will sweep the other agent's in-flight files into your commit. **Always
`git add android/` (or `ios/`) by explicit pathspec**, never `-A`. Device-route backend lives in
the `papercup` tree (git-sync owns it); the mobile app is this separate repo.

Backend device routes for the app live at `papercup/packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/`.
See plan [[mobile-apps-revival-redesign-2026-06-05]] (D-002 routes, D-003 5-tab redesign).

papercup dev hosts split into two ports (2026-06-05 release-gate cutover; see
papercup `CLAUDE.md` "Server-side code has no hot-reload"):

- **`:3070` (`papercup-dev-api.service`)** = the GREEN/stable operator, run from
  the **separate release checkout** `papercupai-workspace/papercup-release`,
  pinned to the `ready` ref. Restarting it just reboots the same green snapshot —
  your edits in the canonical `papercupai-workspace/papercup` tree are **invisible
  to :3070** until a release-gate deploy (`apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts
  --execute`). I burned time live-verifying a route against :3070 and saw STALE
  behavior because of this.
- **`:3170` (`papercup-staging-api.service`)** = staging, run from `main` (the
  integration tree). To live-verify a server-side edit: `systemctl --user restart
  papercup-staging-api.service`, wait ~30-60s for boot, then probe `:3170`.
- The Tauri dev shell also spawns its operator from the integration tree.

Practical rule: backend edits in the canonical checkout → restart + probe
**:3170**, not :3070. Confirms [[verify-server-pid-before-measuring]] —
always confirm WHICH process/checkout is serving the port before trusting a
live result.

entries.text:
In PostgreSQL a **bare** `ORDER BY <name>` resolves to the **SELECT-list output
column alias** first, not the underlying table column. So a query that casts then
re-aliases under the same name silently changes the sort type:

```sql
SELECT id::text AS id, ...   -- id is now TEXT in the output
FROM harness_shared.agent_activity
ORDER BY id DESC             -- binds to the TEXT alias → LEXICAL sort
```

This sorts the bigint lexicographically: `"999" > "1000" > "1618"`. A read like
this silently **freezes at the last lower-digit value** the instant the id sequence
crosses a digit boundary (999→1000). It looks fine in tests that only use single/
same-digit ids, and a direct psql `ORDER BY id` (no aliasing) is correct, so it hides.

**Fixes (any):** `ORDER BY id::bigint DESC` (expression → binds to the table/input
column, numeric), or qualify: `ORDER BY agent_activity.id DESC`, or don't shadow the
column name in the SELECT alias. A `WHERE id > N` clause is unaffected — WHERE always
binds to the table column, never the output alias — which is the discriminator that
isolates this bug.

Found + fixed 2026-06-05 in `activity:recent`
(`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/activity/recent.ts`), plan
papercusp-worker-integration-2026-06-04 D-014. The curator + pui fleet view seed
from that tool, so both were reading a snapshot frozen at id 999.
entries.description: PG `ORDER BY <bareName>` binds to the SELECT output alias, so `SELECT id::text AS id … ORDER BY id` sorts the bigint LEXICALLY ("999">"1000")

In **Restart**, `import { client } from '@papercusp/db'` is postgres-js 3.4.9 (`postgres(DATABASE_URL)`). Two binding quirks bit P-074's storage.ts (raw tagged-template SQL):

- **`client.json(obj)` throws** `The "string" argument must be of type string ... Received an instance of Object`. → Use `${JSON.stringify(obj)}::jsonb` for jsonb columns instead.
- **A raw `Date` param throws** the same error (`Received an instance of Date`). → Use `${d.toISOString()}` (the column is `timestamp`; the ISO string casts fine).
- text[] columns: pass the JS array with a cast — `${arr}::text[]` (empty `${[]}::text[]` works).

(The papercup **operator** uses a fresh `postgres()` instance + `sql.json()` + raw `Date` happily — so this is specific to Restart's `client`/version, not a universal postgres-js rule.) Verified by isolating each param in a bisect insert. Context: [[project_universal_testing_p074_restart_scout]].

Restart prod (Hetzner `178.156.253.226`, `/opt/Restart`) — two traps when touching prod out-of-band:

1. **The prod git SHA is the deploy marker.** `deploy/deploy.sh` computes which services to
   rebuild by diffing prod's `git rev-parse HEAD` against local HEAD. If you `git reset`/`pull`
   prod's checkout without rebuilding the affected images, every commit in the skipped range
   silently never deploys (the next deploy diffs from the advanced SHA). Leave the checkout at
   its last-deployed SHA; land changes on `origin/master` for durability and `git apply` just
   your hunk to prod's working tree (the next real deploy's `reset --hard` converges).

2. **Compose-config changes can recreate dependencies.** `docker compose up -d <svc>` recreates
   any dependency whose config changed — e.g. the queued pgvector `postgres` image swap on
   master would recreate the prod DB as a side effect. For targeted env-only restarts use
   `up -d --no-deps <svc>`.

**Why:** On 2026-06-05 prod sat at `d3fa76be` with `origin/master` 10 commits ahead (incl. the
deferred pgvector postgres swap); enabling the search-relevance env on shop-api via a naive
reset would have both poisoned the deploy marker and bounced the prod DB.

**How to apply:** Out-of-band prod fixes = backup `.env.production` → append/edit env →
`git apply` the compose hunk → `up -d --no-deps <svc>` → verify; never `git reset` prod outside
`deploy.sh`. Related: [[Restart project stack]].
entries.description: Restart deploy.sh uses prod's git SHA as its changed-service marker — never advance /opt/Restart's checkout without rebuilding; for env-only changes, hand-apply hunks + `up -d --no-deps <svc>`

entries.text:
## Two complementary error logs

**1. `toastLog` (server-side, PG)** — every call to `toast.error()` / `addToast()`. Pull via:

```sh
curl -sS "http://localhost:3055/api/zero-harness/rest-query?name=toastLog.recent&args=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%7D" \
  | jq -r '.rows[] | "\(.createdAt | tonumber / 1000 | strftime("%H:%M:%S")) [\(.level)] \(.message)"'
```

Schema: `{id, level, message, description, harnessSlug, createdAt, actionLabel, actionHref}`. Timestamps are UTC.

**Use this first** when debugging "is the console clean?" / "what errors did the user see?". `tauri-agent-tools console-monitor --duration N` only captures logs fired DURING the N-second window — anything from page load, prior session, or earlier in the same session is invisible. The persistent toastLog has all of it.

Useful query patterns:
- Last N errors: `.rows[] | select(.level == "error")`
- Distinct messages: `.rows[].message | sed 's/[0-9]\\+/N/g' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` to see frequency
- Since timestamp: filter by `createdAt > <ms>`

When chasing user-reported errors with no live reproduction, this is the diagnostic surface for user-facing toasts. Live console-monitor is for verifying a fix took effect *after* you find a recent error.

## 2. `window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events` (client-side, localStorage)

The vitals-recorder in `apps/operator/app/admin/testing/_lib/vitals-recorder.ts` patches `console.error` + `window.error` + `unhandledrejection` and persists to `localStorage['papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1']`.

**Scope caveat:** `PerfObserverProvider` (which calls `startRecorder()`) only mounts on `/admin/testing` pages. On every other route `window.__papercuspPerfRecorder` is `undefined` and querying `events.length` returns 0 vacuously — **not a valid "console is clean" signal for `/setup`, `/harness`, `/marketplace`, etc.** For those routes use `tauri-agent-tools capture -o <dir>` and read `<dir>/console-errors.json` — that taps WebKit's devtools console directly and catches React hook errors, "Fetch API cannot load … due to access control checks", chunk-load failures, etc. This is what captures:
- React errors ("Rendered more hooks…", hydration errors)
- ChunkLoadError, module/compile errors (Turbopack/SWC parse failures)
- Unhandled promise rejections
- Anything else that hits `console.error` but doesn't write a user toast

Query via `tauri-agent-tools eval`:
```js
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1') || '[]')
  .filter(e => e.kind === 'console-error' || e.kind === 'unhandled-error')
```

Grouping by `e.detail.slice(0, 80)` collapses repeated identical errors into a count.

### Clearing the perf log

The recorder keeps an in-memory `events` array AND flushes to localStorage. `localStorage.removeItem` alone doesn't work — the next `flushToStorage` writes the in-memory copy back. Reset both atomically:

```js
if (window.__papercuspPerfRecorder) window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events = [];
localStorage.removeItem('papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1');
location.reload();
```

### When to use which

- **User-reported "I got a toast that said X"** → toastLog
- **User-reported "got a React error / nothing loads / hook error / chunk error"** → perf recorder (these never hit toastLog)
- **Both are durable across reloads** — toastLog over server restarts too; perf recorder until the user clears localStorage

## 3. `tauri-agent-tools console-monitor` (live bridge stream)

WebKit logs some categories of errors **directly to the devtools console without going through `console.error`** — they're invisible to BOTH toastLog and the perf recorder. Specifically:

- `Fetch API cannot load X due to access control checks` (often a *timeout*, not CORS)
- `Load failed` on fetches that WebKit aborted before resolution
- Network-layer warnings (mixed content, certificate, etc.)

These show up in the bridge's `console-monitor --level error --json` because the bridge taps the webview's *entire* console feed, not just JS calls. So when chasing user-reported "Fetch API cannot load" errors:

```sh
tauri-agent-tools console-monitor --port <port> --token <tok> --duration 30000 --json --level error > /tmp/cm.json
```

…and reload the page during the window. Catches what the other two surfaces don't.

**`"Fetch API cannot load X due to access control checks"` is misleading — on WebKitGTK it almost always means the fetch timed out (Next dev lazy-compile slowness), not real CORS.** Always check `curl -w "%{time_total}"` against the same URL before chasing ACAO headers. Fix is pre-warming routes via `instrumentation-node.ts` register hook.

## Summary: trichotomy of error surfaces

| Surface | Catches | Misses |
|---|---|---|
| `toastLog.recent` | `toast.error()` / `addToast()` | Everything else |
| `__papercuspPerfRecorder` | JS-side `console.error`/`window.error`/rejections | WebKit's direct devtools logs |
| `console-monitor` (bridge) | Entire webview console feed | Anything before its start |

For "is the console clean now?" query *all three* and reconcile.
entries.description: Operator has TWO persistent error logs — toastLog (PG) for user-facing toasts AND window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events (localStorage) for raw console errors / unhandled rejections / compile errors. Query both.
